data.title: Cross-Platform P2P Wi-Fi: How the EU Killed AWDL
data.author: stusmall
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了欧盟《数字市场法》(DMA)如何迫使苹果放弃其专有的Apple Wireless Direct Link (AWDL)协议，转向支持行业标准的Wi-Fi Aware（也称为Neighbor Awareness Networking, NAN）。这一转变意味着iPhone和Android设备将首次能够通过本地无线网络实现真正的跨平台P2P连接。

文章回顾了Wi-Fi P2P技术的发展历史，从早期的Wi-Fi Ad-hoc模式、Wi-Fi Direct到苹果的AWDL，以及现在的Wi-Fi Aware。AWDL是苹果为解决Wi-Fi Direct不足而开发的专有协议，支持如AirDrop和AirPlay等功能。然而，DMA要求苹果在iOS 19中支持Wi-Fi Aware 4.0，并在后续版本中支持5.0，这将迫使AWDL退役。

这一变化对开发者意义重大，因为它将使第三方设备和应用能够使用与苹果内部协议同等高效的P2P Wi-Fi功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Wi-Fi P2P/Wi-Fi Aware技术在Linux等平台上的支持与应用，以及相关技术（如DECT NR+和苹果的Wi-Fi Aware）的现状与未来发展。

不同观点：
• **jauntywundrkind**：对Wi-Fi P2P（Wi-Fi Aware）技术在Linux上的缺乏文档和支持表示失望，认为需要更多的自主连接手段，特别是在当前环境下。强调现有P2P文件共享应用通常假设用户已设置好网络。
• **teleforce**：提出IEEE Wi-Fi联盟的竞争对手3GPP引入了新的p2p mesh无线技术DECT NR+，指出该技术支持实时语音流量，并认为这是一项重要的新标准。
• **tambre**：指出在MT7925上不支持ad-hoc IBSS模式，且Wi-Fi Aware在Linux上的支持信息很少，提到2023年内核提交和一些相关命令。
• **simfoo**：对WiFi Aware在Android之外的文档缺乏表示关注，并询问如何在Raspberry Pi等设备上使用该技术，特别是与Android手机连接。
• **apitman**：通过个人经历说明本地优先网络（如Wi-Fi Aware）可能有助于恢复LAN游戏等本地网络功能，并希望有可靠的API供开发者使用。
• **lawlessone**：引用欧盟互操作性路线图，指出苹果被要求支持Wi-Fi Aware 4.0和5.0，并质疑为何不同时支持AWDL。
• **dwaite**：指出苹果已经支持Wi-Fi Aware，特别是对于ISO 18013-5等标准，并询问是否是关于版本升级或API表面增加。
• **mschuster91**：关注认证和授权问题，特别是在macOS和三星设备上的简化操作，并询问未来如何解决这一问题。

补充讨论：
• **Eduard**：反驳Wi-Fi Ad-hoc未广泛使用的观点，指出在2000年代早期，由于Wi-Fi基站稀缺且昂贵，Ad-hoc模式曾被广泛使用。
• **jokoon**：认为欧盟强制美国公司（如Apple）支持某些标准可能是因为美国监管机构不作为，并指出这可能对消费者有利。
• **formerly_proven和yapyap**：提到技术实现中的具体问题（如网站性能和Apple独占功能），但未深入讨论技术细节。

争议焦点：
• **Wi-Fi Aware技术在Linux和其他非Android平台上的支持不足**，特别是文档和实际应用的缺乏。
• **苹果被要求支持Wi-Fi Aware 4.0和5.0**，以及是否可能继续支持AWDL。
• **认证和授权问题**，特别是在跨设备和跨平台的情况下如何简化和统一操作。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕Wi-Fi P2P/Wi-Fi Aware技术的支持现状、技术挑战和未来发展方向。

Cross-Platform P2P Wi-Fi: How the EU Killed AWDL
This post investigates how we got from Wi-Fi Direct to AWDL to Wi-Fi Aware, what makes Wi-Fi Aware technically superior, and why this shift unlocks true cross-platform peer-to-peer connectivity for developers.
Adam Fish
Founder and CEO
TL;DR:
Under pressure from the EUâs Digital Markets Act (DMA), Apple is being forced to ditch its proprietary peer-to-peer Wi-Fi protocol â Apple Wireless Direct Link (AWDL) â in favor of the industry-standard Wi-Fi Aware, also known as Neighbor Awareness Networking (NAN). A quietly published EU interoperability roadmap mandates Apple support Wi-Fi Aware 4.0 in iOS 19 and v5.0,
1
thereafter, essentially forcing AWDL into retirement. This post investigates how we got here (from Wi-Fi Direct to AWDL to Wi-Fi Aware), what makes Wi-Fi Aware technically superior, and why this shift unlocks true cross-platform peer-to-peer connectivity for developers.
EU Forces Appleâs Hand on Peer-to-Peer Wi-Fi
In a little-publicized mandate, the European Commission explicitly requires Apple to implement the Wi-Fi Allianceâs Wi-Fi Aware standard as part of DMA interoperability measures. The official DMA roadmap states:
âApple shall implement the measures for Wi-Fi Aware 4.0 in the next major iOS release, i.e. iOS 19, at the latest, and for Wi-Fi Aware 5.0 in the next iOS release at the latest nine months following the introduction of the Wi-Fi Aware 5.0 specificationâ
In plain terms, by the time iOS 19 ships, iPhones must support Wi-Fi Aware v4.0, and Apple must roll out v5.0 support soon after the Wi-Fi Alliance finalizes that spec.
Crucially, this decision was not a voluntary announcement by Apple â it was imposed by regulators. Apple has kept quiet about these changes publicly, likely because they involve opening up formerly closed-off tech. The DMA enforcement timeline was highlighted in an EU Q&A site and legal annex, not an Apple press release.
7
The European Commissionâs language makes it clear this is about enabling third-party devices and apps to use high-bandwidth peer-to-peer (P2P) Wi-Fi features equal to Appleâs own, rather than Apple benevolently adopting a new standard. In fact, the EU order compels Apple to deprecate AWD
L
and ensure third-party solutions using Wi-Fi Aware are just as effective as Appleâs internal protocols. In short, the EU gave Apple no choice: embrace Wi-Fi Aware or face penalties.
What does this mean? Essentially, Appleâs hidden sauce for fast device-to-device communication â AWDL â is being forced into retirement. And with that, for the first time, iPhones and Androids will speak a common language for local wireless networking. Letâs unpack how we got here, and why itâs a big deal for developers.
From Wi-Fi Direct to AWDL to Wi-Fi Aware: A Brief History
To understand the significance, we need a quick history of ad-hoc Wi-Fi protocols:
Wi-Fi Ad-hoc (IBSS mode):
Early 802.11 allowed devices to connect directly in a peer-to-peer âad-hocâ network (IBSS), but it had limitations (no always-on discovery, no power-saving coordination, weak security). It never gained widespread use.
Wi-Fi Direct:
The Wi-Fi Allianceâs first big attempt at standard P2P. Wi-Fi Direct (circa 2010) allows devices to form a direct link without an AP, designating one device as a group owner (soft AP) for security and IP allocation. It improved on ad-hoc mode (supporting WPA2, dynamic group formation), but had drawbacks â e.g. limited service discovery capabilities and difficulty staying connected to infrastructure Wi-Fi concurrently.
Apple Wireless Direct Link (AWDL):
Around 2014, Apple developed AWDL as a proprietary, high-performance P2P Wi-Fi protocol for its ecosystem. According to Appleâs patent on AWDL (US20180083858A1) and reverse-engineering by researchers, AWDL was designed to address Wi-Fi Directâs concerns and succeeded ad-hoc IBSS mode.
8
Apple deployed AWDL in over a billion devices (every modern iPhone, iPad, Mac) to power AirDrop, AirPlay peer connections, GameKit, Apple Watch unlock, and more.
8,9
Notably, AWDL can coexist with regular Wi-Fi by rapidly hopping channels â an iPhone can be on an AP and seamlessly switch to AWDL channel windows to talk to a peer.
9
This gave AWDL low latency and high throughput without dropping your internet connection.
Neighbor Awareness Networking (NAN / Wi-Fi Aware):
As it turns out, Apple didnât keep all of AWDL to itself â it contributed to the Wi-Fi Alliance, which adopted AWDLâs approach as the basis for the NAN standard (branded âWi-Fi Awareâ) around 2015.
8
Wi-Fi Aware is essentially the industry-standard cousin of AWDL, enabling devices to discover each other and communicate directly with Wi-Fi speeds, in a power-efficient way, regardless of vendor. Android added platform support for Wi-Fi Aware in Oreo (8.0) and later,
10
but Apple until now stuck with its in-house AWDL stack which can be us

data.title: Postgres Language Server: Initial Release
data.author: steinroe
data.article_summary: **Postgres Language Server** 是一个为 Postgres 提供语言工具和实现语言服务器协议（LSP）的项目，旨在提升开发者体验和提供可靠的 SQL 工具。该项目基于 Postgres 自身的解析器 **libpg_query**，确保 100% 的语法兼容性。它采用客户端-服务器架构，具有传输无关的设计，可以通过 LSP、CLI、HTTP API 或 WebAssembly 模块访问功能。主要特性包括自动补全、语法错误高亮、类型检查（通过 **EXPLAIN**）和受 **Squawk** 启发的 linter。项目当前专注于优化核心功能，并欢迎社区贡献。更多详情和贡献机会可查看项目的问题和讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres Language Server的发布及其功能、应用场景和实现技术细节

不同观点：
• [支持与赞赏] 多名用户（如casper14、0xa2、stevage等）对该项目的发布表示兴奋和赞赏，并计划试用。
• [应用场景的疑问] stevage对"Postgres development"的具体使用场景感到困惑，质疑该工具是为编写存储过程还是复杂查询的人设计的。
• [技术实现细节] juleswritescode详细介绍了SQL文件解析中的技术挑战，解释了使用两个解析器（libpg_query和tree-sitter）来处理不同状态的SQL语句。
• [对工作流的支持] bitbasher和Pedro_Ribeiro询问了该工具对非.sql文件中SQL编写的支持情况，如在Go或Rust代码中嵌入SQL的场景。
• [集成与扩展] edg5000和Pedro_Ribeiro进一步探讨了该工具在不同编程语言中的集成，如在多行字符串中嵌入SQL语句时的静态检查和自动补全功能。

补充讨论：
• [现有工具的比较] 一些用户（如vendiddy和ninetyninenine）提到了现有工具如DBeaver、JetBrains的优缺点，并对Postgres缺乏良好的IDE体验表示遗憾。
• [格式化功能] t1mmen关注了项目是否会加入格式化功能，特别是对存储过程的格式化支持。
• [浏览器内使用] matus_congrady询问了该工具在浏览器内通过monaco-editor使用的可能性和示例。
• [迁移文件管理] tmountain提到该工具对通过迁移文件管理PL/pgSQL代码的人来说是一个重大改变，并分享了一个相关项目链接。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在该工具的应用场景（是为复杂查询还是存储过程设计）以及其在不同开发工作流中的集成和扩展能力。

Postgres Language Server
A collection of language tools and a Language Server Protocol (LSP) implementation for Postgres, focusing on developer experience and reliable SQL tooling.
Docs:
pgtools.dev
Install:
instructions
CLI releases
VSCode
Neovim
Overview
This project provides a toolchain for Postgres development, built on Postgres' own parser
libpg_query
to ensure 100% syntax compatibility. It is built on a Server-Client architecture with a transport-agnostic design. This means all features can be accessed not only through the
Language Server Protocol
, but also through other interfaces like a CLI, HTTP APIs, or a WebAssembly module. The goal is to make all the great Postgres tooling out there as accessible as possible, and to build anything that is missing ourselves.
The following features are implemented:
Autocompletion
Syntax Error Highlighting
Type-checking (via
EXPLAIN
error insights)
Linter, inspired by
Squawk
Our current focus is on refining and enhancing these core features while building a robust and easily accessible infrastructure. For future plans and opportunities to contribute, please check out the issues and discussions. Any contributions are welcome!
Contributors
psteinroe
juleswritescode
Acknowledgements
A big thanks to the following projects, without which this project wouldn't have been possible:
libpg_query
: For extracting the Postgres' parser
Biome
: For implementing a toolchain infrastructure we could copy from
Squawk
: For the linter inspiration

data.title: Koto Programming Language
data.author: virtualritz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种用于Rust应用的轻量级脚本语言。该语言旨在简化Rust程序中的脚本编写，提供更灵活的动态执行能力。文章提供了相关文档和安装指南，帮助开发者快速上手。同时，还设有一个在线编程环境（Playground），方便用户直接在浏览器中测试和运行脚本。这种语言有助于提升Rust项目的开发效率，特别适用于需要频繁修改和调试的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Koto语言的评价与比较，以及与Lua、Rhai等其他脚本语言的差异和应用场景。

不同观点：
• [aerzen] 认为Koto在"由一个疯子编写的代码可读性"这一非正式指标上优于Rhai，但未必优于Lua。
• [chaosprint] 表示Rhai的语法更直接，并通过实际应用（如实时音频处理）展示了Rhai的优势。
• [mostafah] 赞赏Koto的高层次功能扩展，并希望像Lua这样的通用脚本语言能更广泛使用。
• [tzury] 分享了使用Lua扩展Nginx和Envoy-proxy的经验，表明Lua在实际项目中的应用。
• [account-5] 建议如果选择与Rust配合的脚本语言，更倾向于Nushell的语法。
• [fstarship] 认为大多数脚本语言采用鸭子/动态类型，但推崇Rust的推断类型和更健壮的特性，希望有一种带有垃圾收集器的Rust-like语言。

补充讨论：
• [irh] 作为Koto的创建者，参与讨论并表示愿意回答问题，显示了开发者对反馈的开放态度。
• [esafak] 关注Koto是否能快速编译以用于shell脚本。
• [shahriarhus] 将Koto与C++的Lua进行比较，提出了语言之间的相似性问题。
• [fithisux] 和 [amadoury] 对Koto名称的趣味性进行了评论，而非技术性讨论。
• [mentalgear] 赞赏Koto的简洁语法，但希望它有类型支持。
• [seivan] 对Koto的文档和与Rust的整合表示赞赏，但希望它有更好的静态类型和类似Elixir的功能。

争议焦点：
• Koto与Rhai、Lua等其他脚本语言的优劣比较，特别是在语法简洁性和功能扩展方面的不同看法。
• 对脚本语言是否应采用静态类型或动态类型的讨论，反映了不同开发者对类型系统的偏好和需求差异。

- **bknd/elements**: 认证和媒体的React组件。

⭐ Live Demo
bknd simplifies app development by providing a fully functional backend for database management, authentication, media and workflows. Being lightweight and built on Web Standards, it can be deployed nearly anywhere, including running inside your framework of choice. No more deploying multiple separate services!
For documentation and examples, please visit
https://docs.bknd.io
.
Warning
Please keep in mind that
bknd
is still under active development
and therefore full backward compatibility is not guaranteed before reaching v1.0.0.
Size
The size on npm is misleading, as the
bknd
package includes the backend, the ui components as well as the whole backend bundled into the cli including static assets.
Depending on what you use, the size can be higher as additional dependencies are getting pulled in. The minimal size of a full
bknd
app as an API is around 212 kB gzipped (e.g. deployed as Cloudflare Worker).
Motivation
Creating digital products always requires developing both the backend (the logic) and the frontend (the appearance). Building a backend from scratch demands deep knowledge in areas such as authentication and database management. Using a backend framework can speed up initial development, but it still requires ongoing effort to work within its constraints (e.g.,
"how to do X with Y?"
), which can quickly slow you down. Choosing a backend system is a tough decision, as you might not be aware of its limitations until you encounter them.
The solution:
A backend system that only assumes and implements primitive details, integrates into multiple environments, and adheres to industry standards.
Features
⚡ Instant backend with full REST API:
Data
: Define, query, and control your data with ease.
Auth
: Easily implement reliable authentication strategies.
Media
: Effortlessly manage and serve all your media files.
Flows
: Design and run workflows with seamless automation. (UI integration coming soon!)
🌐 Built on Web Standards for maximum compatibility
🏃‍♂️ Multiple run modes
standalone using the CLI
using a JavaScript runtime (Node, Bun, workerd)
using a React framework (Next.js, React Router, Astro)
📦 Official API and React SDK with type-safety
⚛️ React elements for auto-configured authentication and media components

data.title: Every Flop Counts: Scaling a 300B LLM Without Premium GPUs
data.author: bretpiatt
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在大规模训练混合专家（Mixture of Experts, MoE）模型时克服成本和资源限制的方法。作者提出了两种MoE大型语言模型（LLM）：Ling-Lite（168亿参数，激活参数27.5亿）和Ling-Plus（2900亿参数，激活参数288亿）。这些模型在性能上可媲美行业领先的标准，且通过优化架构、训练过程和异常处理等方法，显著降低了训练成本。特别地，在低性能设备上预训练3000亿参数的MoE LLM，计算成本减少了约20%。实验结果表明，这种方法能够在资源受限的环境下实现高效、可扩展的AI开发。模型和相关数据可在一个指定网址访问。

Abstract:
In this technical report, we tackle the challenges of training large-scale Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, focusing on overcoming cost inefficiency and resource limitations prevalent in such systems. To address these issues, we present two differently sized MoE large language models (LLMs), namely Ling-Lite and Ling-Plus (referred to as "Bailing" in Chinese, spelled Bǎilíng in Pinyin). Ling-Lite contains 16.8 billion parameters with 2.75 billion activated parameters, while Ling-Plus boasts 290 billion parameters with 28.8 billion activated parameters. Both models exhibit comparable performance to leading industry benchmarks. This report offers actionable insights to improve the efficiency and accessibility of AI development in resource-constrained settings, promoting more scalable and sustainable technologies. Specifically, to reduce training costs for large-scale MoE models, we propose innovative methods for (1) optimization of model architecture and training processes, (2) refinement of training anomaly handling, and (3) enhancement of model evaluation efficiency. Additionally, leveraging high-quality data generated from knowledge graphs, our models demonstrate superior capabilities in tool use compared to other models. Ultimately, our experimental findings demonstrate that a 300B MoE LLM can be effectively trained on lower-performance devices while achieving comparable performance to models of a similar scale, including dense and MoE models. Compared to high-performance devices, utilizing a lower-specification hardware system during the pre-training phase demonstrates significant cost savings, reducing computing costs by approximately 20%. The models can be accessed at

43460455.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在大规模训练混合专家（Mixture of Experts, MoE）模型时克服成本和资源限制的方法。作者提出了两种MoE大型语言模型（LLM）：Ling-Lite（168亿参数，激活参数27.5亿）和Ling-Plus（2900亿参数，激活参数288亿）。这些模型在性能上可媲美行业领先的标准，且通过优化架构、训练过程和异常处理等方法，显著降低了训练成本。特别地，在低性能设备上预训练3000亿参数的MoE LLM，计算成本减少了约20%。实验结果表明，这种方法能够在资源受限的环境下实现高效、可扩展的AI开发。模型和相关数据可在一个指定网址访问。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为“Real-Time Chess”的项目，它重新设计了传统国际象棋，取消了轮流走棋的概念，允许玩家随时移动棋子。为了避免混乱，每个棋子都有独立的冷却时间，期间不能再次移动。项目实现了一个物理棋盘，通过电磁铁和显示器来跟踪和展示每个棋子的冷却时间，防止作弊。棋盘的设计文件和固件代码已在GitHub上开源，采用MIT许可证。项目还列出了一些已知问题，如电源分配、装配公差和引脚高度等，并提供了可能的解决方案。该项目旨在提高象棋的趣味性和观赏性。

Real Time Chess
A physical chess board without the concept of turns
Video explanation:
https://youtu.be/y7VtSK23_Jg
Pitch
Chess is boring. I'm boring too so I enjoy it anyways, but I can't help but think "I could design it better." Normally in chess players move sequentially in turns, but this introduces a huge latency bug that the developers of chess forgot to patch: you spend literally half the time waiting for your opponent!
The obvious solution is just get rid of the concept of turns in chess altogether and let players move whenever they want. Real time strategy games like StarCraft and Age of Empires are much more fun and spectator friendly than chess, so this should be a pretty uncontroversial minor rules update that can be implemented before the next world championship. To prevent things from getting too chaotic over the board each piece has an individual cooldown, so once it's been moved it can't move for a fixed period afterwards.
However there's an unfortunate roadblock to the widespread adoption of real time chess: as the
Niemann controversy
has made all too clear, chess is
not immune
from accusations of cheating through spectator
ass
istance or outside
anal
isys tools. Trying to have players self enforce these piece cooldowns is impossible. However where the intrinsic goodness of the human psyche fails, engineering is always ready to step in. This project is a physical chess board that keeps track and displays the cooldown remaining for each piece, and even physically holds them in place so no accidental cheating can occur.
Design Files
The firmware and pcb kicad files are in this repo. For the physical design, see
the design on OnShape
. Other than those parts that were cnced, here were the off the shelf components used:
Insulating washers
: One under each electromagnet, to keep them isolated from the casing
Plastic screws
: To attach electromagnets to base, plastic to prevent electrical connection
These
and
these
screws: to attach the internal supports and squares respectively
Spacers
: For an offset between the decorative and functional pcbs
Electromagnets
: Most expensive part other than the machining, ~$600 per board. Could probably get them cheaper from China or something but for low quantities this was easiest
Known Issues
Power distribution: Traces on the pcbs are way undersized given there are many amps running through them, so there are large voltage drops when many pieces are on cooldown simultaneously. To solve this these traces should be much wider
Tolerances: The pcbs have extremely tight tolerances which makes assmbling the board extremely annoying. The edges and holes should probably have more room
Pin heights: The height of the pins for the banana connectors are taller than the mechanical design allows for, these are fairly easy to shorten using a dremel but probably something that should be fixed
Corner screws: Given the order of assembly, it's impossible to insert/fasten the 4 corner screws

data.title: Caido – A lightweight web security auditing toolkit
data.author: charlieirish
data.article_summary: Caido是一款轻量级网页安全审计工具，旨在帮助安全专业人员和爱好者高效、简便地进行web应用安全审计。其功能包括实时拦截和查看HTTP请求、重放和自定义请求以测试端点、自动化安全测试、实时网站结构可视化、自动匹配和替换请求、以及自定义编码器/解码器。Caido支持简化的插件系统，允许用户以最少代码扩展工具功能。此外，它采用客户端/服务器架构，可在任何设备或VPS上运行，并提供便捷的项目管理功能。Caido重视用户隐私，使用cookies来改善浏览体验，用户可选择接受所有cookies或仅接受必要cookies。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Caido和Burp Suite的比较与评价

不同观点：
• **alp1n3_eth**：赞赏Caido的免费 tier 允许保存项目，适合个人项目和试验。虽然Caido的UI/UX有待改进，但速度和性能优于Burp Suite，Burp Suite经常出现崩溃和占用过多CPU/RAM的问题。Caido在性能上表现更稳定。
  
• **dfc**：对Burp Suite的感情是既喜欢又有少许不满，认为市场需要更多竞争者。虽然看过ZAP，但觉得它以前只是一个混乱的Burp复制品，前景不明朗。

• **jkmcf**：因为Caido网站上的简洁cookie横幅而对Caido产生好感，并表示会进一步了解。这显示出用户对隐私和用户体验的关注。

补充讨论：
- **竞争与选择**：dfc提到希望有更多工具能与Burp Suite竞争，暗示目前Burp Suite可能在市场上占据主导地位，但并非所有用户都完全满意。
- **性能问题**：alp1n3_eth指出Burp Suite的性能问题，特别是崩溃和资源占用，而Caido在这方面表现较好，这可能成为用户选择Caido的一个重要原因。
- **用户体验**：jkmcf对隐私和简洁用户界面的关注显示出用户在选择工具时，不仅考虑功能性，也重视用户体验和隐私保护。

争议焦点：
- **UI/UX的优劣**：虽然alp1n3_eth和dfc都认为Burp Suite的UI/UX存在问题，但对Caido的UI/UX评价不一，显示出用户在使用体验上的不同期望。

data.title: Typed Japanese
data.author: Philpax
data.article_summary: "Typed Japanese" 是一个基于 TypeScript 类型系统的库，用于学习和表达符合日语语法规则的句子。该项目通过类型系统创建了一种领域特定语言（DSL），允许开发者使用 TypeScript 编译器验证日语句子的正确性。它支持动词和形容词的各种变形形式，并能够处理条件句、指示形式以及短语连接等语法结构。通过这种方法，不仅可以帮助程序员理解日语语法，还可以为人工智能提供一种中间格式，用于分析和验证日语句子的语法。该系统涵盖了日语的主要动词分类（五段动词、一段动词、不规则动词）和形容词分类（い形容词、な形容词），并支持多种变形形式。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• musicale认为古典符号/分析AI（如语法和语义模型）具有可解释性，但无法像现代DNNs那样扩展处理大规模数据。
• makeitdouble提供了对评论中提到的一个日语网络迷因的背景信息链接，帮助不熟悉该迷因的人理解。

补充讨论：
• enricozb提到了Lambek计算，一种用于书面语言的通用类型系统，解释了词可以是函数或具体类型，并且函数可以在左侧或右侧接受参数。
• IshKebab对日语语法的严格性表示惊讶，提出了关于日语语法结构的问题。
• lewisjoe询问是否可以利用相关理论构建日语语法检查器。
• barlog简短地总结了提到的迷因，提供了一个简化的解释。
• guerrilla将讨论与分类语法联系起来，描述了其与简单类型λ演算的相似性，并讨论了方向性、多态性及相关类型理论的发展。他还提到了一些他忘记名字的著名类型理论学者，如Carl H.（可能是指Carl Hewitt或其他人）。

• 古典符号AI与现代DNNs在可解释性和扩展性上的对比，以及如何在实际应用（如日语语法检查器）中应用这些理论。

🌸 Typed Japanese
If you can write TypeScript, you can understand Japanese!
Typed Japanese is a TypeScript type-level library that enables the expression of complete Japanese sentences through the type system. It creates a domain-specific language (DSL) based on Japanese grammar rules, allowing a subset of grammatically correct natural language to be written and verified using TypeScript's compiler.
This project also explores an intermediate format for AI in language learning. For example, LLMs could return grammar analysis of Japanese sentences using this format instead of JSON, enabling verification through TypeScript's type checker to improve correctness.
📖
Want to learn more?
Check out our
detailed blog post
which explains how the TypeScript type system can be used to learn Japanese grammar from the ground up. The article starts with basic programming concepts and gradually builds up to complex Japanese grammatical structures like conditional sentences and interrogative phrases.
// Define the proper noun "ヒンメル"
type
ヒンメル
=
ProperNoun
<
"ヒンメル"
>
;
// Define する verb
type
する
=
IrregularVerb
&
{
dictionary
:
"する"
}
;
// Create the そうした pattern (past form of そうする)
type
そうした
=
DemonstrativeAction
<
Demonstrative
&
"そう"
,
する
,
"た形"
>
;
// Create the conditional phrase "ヒンメルならそうした"
type
ヒンメルならそうした
=
ConditionalPhrase
<
ヒンメル
,
"なら"
,
そうした
>
;
// Type checking examples
const
properExample
:
ヒンメルならそうした
=
"ヒンメルならそうした"
;
// "If it were Himmel, he would do so"
// 如果是辛美尔的话，他也会这么做的
🤖 Verb System
Verb Classes
Japanese verbs are categorized into three main classes:
Godan Verbs (五段動詞)
- Also known as "Group 1" or "u-verbs"
Endings: う, く, ぐ, す, つ, ぬ, ぶ, む, る
Examples: 話す (hanasu - to speak), 書く (kaku - to write)
Ichidan Verbs (一段動詞)
- Also known as "Group 2" or "ru-verbs"
Always end with る
Examples: 食べる (taberu - to eat), 見る (miru - to see)
Irregular Verbs (不規則動詞)
- Only two main verbs
する (suru - to do)
来る (kuru - to come)
Verb Conjugation Forms
The system supports these conjugation forms:
辞書形 (Dictionary form)
ます形 (Polite form)
て形 (Te form)
た形 (Past form)
ない形 (Negative form)
可能形 (Potential form)
受身形 (Passive form)
使役形 (Causative form)
意向形 (Volitional form)
命令形 (Imperative form)
条件形 (Conditional form)
仮定形 (Hypothetical form)
type
買う
=
GodanVerb
&
{
stem
:
"買"
;
ending
:
"う"
}
;
type
買うて形
=
ConjugateVerb
<
買う
,
"て形"
>
;
// 買って
type
買うた形
=
ConjugateVerb
<
買う
,
"た形"
>
;
// 買った
type
食べる
=
IchidanVerb
&
{
stem
:
"食べ"
;
ending
:
"る"
}
;
type
食べるて形
=
ConjugateVerb
<
食べる
,
"て形"
>
;
// 食べて
type
食べるた形
=
ConjugateVerb
<
食べる
,
"た形"
>
;
// 食べた
🎨 Adjective System
Japanese adjectives are categorized into two main classes:
I-Adjectives (い形容詞)
- End with い
Examples: いい (good), 楽しい (fun), 高い (expensive)
Na-Adjectives (な形容詞)
- Require な when modifying nouns
Examples: 綺麗 (pretty), 静か (quiet), 好き (liked)
Adjective Conjugation Forms
The system supports these conjugation forms for adjectives:
基本形 (Basic form)
丁寧形 (Polite form)
過去形 (Past form)
否定形 (Negative form)
type
いい
=
IAdjective
&
{
stem
:
"い"
;
ending
:
"い"
;
irregular
:
true
}
;
type
綺麗
=
NaAdjective
&
{
stem
:
"綺麗"
}
;
📚 Phrase and Sentence Composition
The system now supports:
Adjectives and verbs with particles
Connecting phrases with Japanese punctuation
Basic sentence structures
Conditional expressions with particles like なら
Demonstrative forms with actions
Example: Connecting simple adjective and imperative verb phrases
// I-adjective "ii" (good) with irregular conjugation
// Then add particle "yo" to basic form of "ii" -> "ii yo"
type
いい
=
IAdjective
&
{
stem
:
"い"
;
ending
:
"い"
;
irregular
:
true
}
;
type
いいよ
=
PhraseWithParticle
<
ConjugateAdjective
<
いい
,
"基本形"
>
,
"よ"
>
;
// Irregular verb "kuru" (to come)
// Then add particle "yo" to imperative form of "kuru" -> "koi yo"
type
来る
=
IrregularVerb
&
{
dictionary
:
"来る"
}
;
type
来いよ
=
PhraseWithParticle
<
ConjugateVerb
<
来る
,
"命令形"
>
,
"よ"
>
;
// Connect both phrases -> "ii yo, koi yo"
type
いいよ来いよ
=
ConnectedPhrases
<
いいよ
,
来いよ
>
;
// Type checking examples
const
correctPhrase1
:
いいよ
=
"いいよ"
;
// "It's good!" (114)
const
correctPhrase2
:
来いよ
=
"来いよ"
;
// "Come here!" (514)
const
correctFullPhrase
:
いいよ来いよ
=
"いいよ、来いよ"
;
// "It's good, come here!"

data.author: pcfwik
data.article_summary: 《Paged Out!》杂志第6期发布，共有80页，包含丰富的文章和艺术作品。本期封面由艺术家Ninja Jo创作。由于菜单脚本问题，发布略有延迟，但团队成功解决。目前尚未提供印刷版，但正在努力测试。作者希望未来增加更多技术类文章，如游戏漏洞和无线电技巧，欢迎投稿至gynvael@pagedout.institute。第5期回顾中提到改进菜单和内容对齐，增加赞助广告以实现自给自足，并计划推出印刷版。第4期扩展了艺术和Demoscene主题，尽管因PDF问题延迟发布，但团队对结果满意。读者可前往官网下载各期杂志并投稿至下一期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一份在线杂志的内容、排版、安全性及其它相关问题的多角度评价和建议

不同观点：
• **内容深度与排版问题**：
   - [ngneer] 认为杂志的文章由于每篇文章只有一页，内容过于简略，只能作为话题的简单引入，无法深入探讨。同时，排版风格多变，导致视觉疲劳，建议考虑使用像Overleaf这样的工具来优化排版。
   - [laacz] 则关注阅读体验，指出在电脑上阅读时，页面需要上下滚动或缩小页面才能看清内容，对视力不友好。

• **排版工具的建议**：
   - [ngneer] 提到LaTeX对某些作者不友好，建议使用像Overleaf这样的工具，以达到内容质量与排版美观的平衡。

• **安全性问题**：
   - [GICodeWarrior] 指出杂志中的一篇文章示例可能存在XSS攻击风险，强调在Django中输出用户提供的内容时需要正确编码以防止安全漏洞。

• **艺术风格与政治立场**：
   - [vindex10] 喜欢杂志的插图风格（人工绘制而非AI生成），但表示不支持使用生活在俄罗斯的艺术家的插图，认为在当前政治环境下应选择其他国家的艺术家。

• **特定内容评价与兴趣**：
   - [okincilleb] 特别喜欢“Spotting Quacks with Puzzles”一文，认为其在提高媒体素养方面非常独特且及时。
   - [4ndrewl] 认为杂志有1980年代Crash杂志的风格，充满怀旧感。
   - [who-shot-jr] 和 [parentheses] 对杂志中关于AI的内容表示赞赏。

• **贡献与参与**：
   - [claytonwramsey] 表示曾收到过投稿邀请但当时没时间参与，表示下次会准备更好的内容。
   - [tiniuclx] 自豪地提到自己撰写的文章被收录在杂志中，显示出对参与该杂志的积极态度。

• **阅读形式与发行方式**：
   - [VladVladikoff] 询问是否可以订购纸质版杂志，而不仅仅是在线下载和自行打印，显示出对纸质版的兴趣。
   - [nickthegreek] 表示在浏览杂志时因内容丰富而暂时停下，但计划稍后继续阅读。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者如[ArcHound] 和 [PaulRobinson] 表达了对杂志整体的喜爱，并认为这种形式的杂志非常有必要存在。
• 总体来看，讨论的焦点集中在内容深度、排版与视觉体验、安全性及艺术作品的政治立场上，同时也有读者对杂志的发行形式提出建议。

43517375.article_content:
Paged Out! Institute Blog
Paged Out! #6 is out!
Download Issue #6 on the
Issues page
. As always, we have cover-art wallpapers too—this time made by the amazing
Ninja Jo (Katerina Belikova)
!
We meet yet again! Writing this blog post is the last thing I do before a new Issue is pushed out. So when I write these words all the work has been done, all the problems have been solved (or put on the "do this when we have time" TODO list), and most of our Institute is already relaxing (i.e. busy with other stuff) and eagerly awaiting the publication. It's also when all the stress related to trying to finalize the Issue goes away and the happiness related to publishing a new issue sets in. So what I'm saying, is that I feel really happy right now to be able to pass Issue #6 into your hands, and really grateful to our team for what they accomplished with this Issue.
And this Issue is objectively the best Issue up to date! It's a total of 80 pages, with A LOT of absolutely amazing articles and art. Actually one of the delaying factors was that our Menu (Table of Content) script broke again and had to be fixed before pushing the Issue out. It's a good problem to have.
We still don't have the print files / option to buy a printed edition for you – blame the stupid flu/cold season for this (
please insert some swear words you like here
). We're close, but I still want to order some test prints myself before we start offering these.
Another thing which I personally want to develop more in Paged Out!, is sourcing articles from the following genres: technical explanations of game glitches (think: speedrunning or movement techniques), technical demoscene tricks, and technical radio/HAM/etc. If you have any solid leads or contact in these communities, please hit me up at
gynvael@pagedout.institute
.
And now, go and enjoy Issue #6! And as usual, the
call for articles for Issue #7 is open!
29 March 2025 / Gynvael
Paged Out! #5 is out!
Download Issue #5 on the
Issues page
. As always, we have cover-art wallpapers too—this time made by the amazing
Mark Graham Artist
!
You know what's the best birthday present a Paged Out! lead can get? A new issue of Paged Out!—hell yeah! And a non-beta build at that. There are countless improvements over #4, including a better menu,
a lot
of alignment fixes literally everywhere, better support for long titles, and so on. This said, if you spot any problems, please let us know—there are less of them now and, as such, they are harder to find.
You'll also notice there are a few more Sponsorship Ads this time around. As you might remember, originally we had a policy of having only one ad page per ten content pages. Then the policy changed to round that number up—so for 51 pages, there would be 6 pages of ads. Even with that change, however, we were still in the red with regard to costs. And, as you might also remember, another goal of Paged Out! is to make it self-sustainable (i.e., make it pay its own bills). As such, I made the call to change the ad policy once again and remove the limit altogether. This doesn't mean PO! will be flooded with ads now—I will always try to include the minimum number of ads necessary to ensure PO! isn't in the red (or isn't so much in the red that it becomes a problem). But yes, there are a couple more ads in this issue (9 pages instead of 6 under the old policy).
The next steps for us are (in somewhat random order): rebuilding previous issues with the new engine (to non-beta ones), getting print-ready PDFs in your hands (we are really close to this), and launching the ability to buy Paged Out! from print-on-demand websites (we’re pretty excited about this one, and some test issues have already been printed).
And now, go and enjoy Issue #5! And as usual, the
call for articles for Issue #6 is open!
(and we have actually already received the first submission yestarday – that was fast).
19 November 2024 / Gynvael
Paged Out! #4 is out!
Download Issue #4 on the
Issues page
. As always, we have cover-art wallpapers too – this time made by our returning artist from Issue #1 –
ReFiend
!
One thing we're supper happy with is the expansion to new topics – or rather topics we always wanted to have but never got article submissions for. So with Issue #4 we welcome the "Art" category with amazing pixel and digital art, as well as "Demoscene", which is something I was always excited about!
As usual, this is a Beta1 build, meaning there are some known issues, which we'll slowly work to fix. For example, we know that some links work in some PDFs viewers, but not in other PDF viewers (e.g. KDE Okular seems to have some issues). Our DTP programmer – foxtrot_charlie – mentioned he'll write something about all the headaches of dealing with PDFs, and there are a lot of these. As you know we had a few-day slipup with publication date due to this – sorry about that! Amusingly we had to re-work the cover in the last moment to change as "May" changed into "June" ;).
Enough said – go and enjoy

Watch All of the Commercials That David Lynch Has Directed: A Big 30-Minute Compilation
in
Film
,
Television
|   	July 16th, 2018
Leave a Comment
Some film­mak­ers start in com­mer­cials, hon­ing their chops in antic­i­pa­tion of mak­ing per­son­al projects lat­er. A select few go in the oth­er direc­tion, real­iz­ing their dis­tinc­tive vision before field­ing offers from com­pa­nies who want a piece of that vision’s cul­tur­al cur­ren­cy. Any­one who’s seen David Lynch’s most acclaimed work will sus­pect, cor­rect­ly, that Lynch belongs in the lat­ter group. With 1977’s cult hit
Eraser­head
, he showed cin­e­ma what it means to be
Lynchi­an
. This brought him the atten­tion of Hol­ly­wood, lead­ing to the respectable suc­cess of
The Ele­phant Man
and the dis­as­ter that was
Dune
. Only in 1986, with
Blue Vel­vet
, could Lynch make a tru­ly, even trou­bling­ly per­son­al film that hit the zeit­geist at just the right moment.
Nat­u­ral­ly, Madi­son Avenue came call­ing soon there­after. “With the smash
Blue Vel­vet
, a Palme d’or at Cannes for
Wild at Heart
, and then the nation­al phe­nom­e­non of
Twin Peaks
’ first sea­son, David Lynch clear­ly estab­lished him­self as the U.S.A.‘s fore­most com­mer­cial­ly viable avant-garde-‘offbeat’ direc­tor,” wrote David Fos­ter Wal­lace in
a 1997 piece on the film­mak­er
.
“For a while there it looked like he might be able to sin­gle-hand­ed­ly bro­ker a new mar­riage between art and com­merce in U.S. movies, open­ing for­mu­la-frozen Hol­ly­wood to some of the eccen­tric­i­ty and vig­or of art film.”
Lynch’s fans in tele­vi­sion adver­tis­ing must have imag­ined that he could do the same for their indus­try, and you can watch the fruits of that hunch in the
half-hour com­pi­la­tion of Lynch-direct­ed com­mer­cials
above.
Lynch has worked for some star­tling­ly big brands, begin­ning with Calvin Klein: his
trio of spots for the fra­grance Obses­sion
take as their basis the writ­ing of F. Scott Fitzger­ald, Ernest Hem­ing­way, and D.H. Lawrence. A few years lat­er he direct­ed a humor­ous
mini-sea­son of
Twin Peaks
to pro­mote Geor­gia Cof­fee
, one of the top brands of canned cof­fee in the Lynch-lov­ing coun­try of Japan. The New York Depart­ment of San­i­ta­tion engaged Lynch’s ser­vices to imbue their anti-lit­ter­ing cam­paign with his sig­na­ture high-con­trast omi­nous­ness, a mood also sought by fash­ion-indus­try titans like Armani, Yves Saint Lau­rent, Guc­ci, and Dior. The mar­keters of hum­bler goods like Alka-Seltzer, Bar­il­la Pas­ta (a seem­ing­ly auteur-aware brand that
has also hired Wim Wen­ders
and
Felli­ni
), and Clear Blue Easy home preg­nan­cy tests have also gone in for a touch of the Lynchi­an.
Quite a few of these com­mer­cials orig­i­nal­ly aired only out­side Amer­i­ca, which may reflect the sup­pos­ed­ly more endur­ing appre­ci­a­tion of Lynch’s work that exists in Europe and Asia. But for all Lynch’s artis­tic dar­ing, the man him­self has always come off as an enthu­si­ast of unre­con­struct­ed Amer­i­can plea­sures. To this day he remains a stead­fast smok­er, and in 1998 brought that per­son­al cred­i­bil­i­ty to the Swiss cig­a­rette brand Parisi­enne. The result­ing spot fea­tures men in ties, show­ers of sparks, dead fish, back­wards talk­ing, a for­bid­ding­ly illu­mi­nat­ed shack, and apoc­a­lyp­tic flames: Parisi­enne, in oth­er words, must have got exact­ly what they paid for.

data.title: Veloren – Voxel action-adventure role-playing
data.author: tete
data.article_summary: Veloren是一款开放世界的动作冒险角色扮演游戏，玩家可在广阔的幻想世界中探索山脉、沙漠、丛林等多种环境。游戏特色包括多样化的武器和战斗风格、与NPC互动、制作装备、挑战 boss 和怪物、以及在程序化生成的世界中冒险。玩家还可以深入地下挖掘矿石，驯服野兽作为伙伴，并支持多人联机。此外，游戏源代码开放，玩家可参与贡献。文章还介绍了最新的开发更新，包括战斗系统改进、新内容添加以及社区贡献者名单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源体素多人游戏Veloren的生成技术、安装问题、游戏设计及发展历程

不同观点：
• **地形生成技术**：[skitter] 解释了Veloren的地形和河流生成基于论文"Large Scale Terrain Generation from Tectonic Uplift and Fluvial Erosion"。地形通过基于噪声的抬升和基于坡度与集水区的侵蚀来生成，河流网络和地形高度决定道路、洞穴和结构的布局。体素只在玩家加载区域时生成，且通常不持久化存储。
• **安装问题与困扰**：[misnome] 提到通过启动器安装时遇到问题，下载的Airshipper版本过旧，且GitHub页面没有最新版本的构建。最终在GitLab上找到最新版本，但对官方链接至GitHub而不是GitLab表示困惑。
• **游戏发展历史**：[dang] 分享了多个关于Veloren的新闻讨论链接，展示了该游戏从2019年到2024年的发展历程和发布版本。
• **游戏改进与体素技术**：[ianbutler] 对Veloren的改进表示赞赏，但质疑为何体素游戏仍然采用基于方块的技术，而不是更接近真实物理交互的画面。并询问这是技术瓶颈还是风格选择。
• **与Cube World的比较**：[matricaria] 提到Veloren类似于Cube World，后者曾被认为是骗局，因其未实现承诺的特性且多年未更新。
• **启动问题解决方案**：[daemonologist] 分享了一些成功启动游戏的经验，包括安装Rust包而非Flatpak或COPR，以及在Wayland下禁用分数缩放等。
• **游戏设计批评**：[littlestymaar] 表示虽然喜欢Veloren的艺术方向和设计目标，但认为缺乏游戏设计师导致游戏体验不佳，许多内容未能达到预期。
• **名称含义**：[pndy] 提到"Veloren"在德语中意为"失落"，并对游戏的生物群落和光照效果表示赞赏。
• **Rust游戏引擎与技术前景**：[echelon] 讨论了Rust在游戏开发中的崛起，提到Veloren使用自研引擎，而Tiny Glade使用Bevy ECS。Bevy和Fyrox引擎各有不同的设计目标和优势，且都开始具备跨平台部署到Web的能力，显示了Rust在游戏开发中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• **正面反馈与个人体验**：[99094] 提到早期体验并高兴看到游戏的进展。[canadiantim] 则表示对游戏的赞赏影响了其工作效率。
• **游戏视觉风格比较**：[muterad_murilax] 提到Veloren让他想起PS3上的3D Dot Game Heroes。

争议焦点：
• **安装问题**：用户[misnome]对安装过程中的版本不一致和官方链接指向问题表示不满。
• **游戏设计与体验**：[littlestymaar]认为Veloren虽然技术上有进步，但在游戏设计上缺乏专业性，导致体验不佳。

总结：Veloren在技术实现和开源发展上获得了较多关注，但在安装体验和游戏设计方面存在一些争议和改进空间。Rust在游戏开发中的应用前景被广泛看好。

• **名称含义**：[pndy] 提到"Veloren"在德语中意为"失落"，并对游戏的生物群落和光照效果表示赞赏。
• **Rust游戏引擎与技术前景**：[echelon] 讨论了Rust在游戏开发中的崛起，提到Veloren使用自研引擎，而Tiny Glade使用Bevy ECS。Bevy和Fyrox引擎各有不同的设计目标和优势，且都开始具备跨平台部署到Web的能力，显示了Rust在游戏开发中的潜力。

补充讨论：
• **正面反馈与个人体验**：[99094] 提到早期体验并高兴看到游戏的进展。[canadiantim] 则表示对游戏的赞赏影响了其工作效率。
• **游戏视觉风格比较**：[muterad_murilax] 提到Veloren让他想起PS3上的3D Dot Game Heroes。

争议焦点：
• **安装问题**：用户[misnome]对安装过程中的版本不一致和官方链接指向问题表示不满。
• **游戏设计与体验**：[littlestymaar]认为Veloren虽然技术上有进步，但在游戏设计上缺乏专业性，导致体验不佳。

总结：Veloren在技术实现和开源发展上获得了较多关注，但在安装体验和游戏设计方面存在一些争议和改进空间。Rust在游戏开发中的应用前景被广泛看好。

data.title: Matrix Calculus (For Machine Learning and Beyond)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了矩阵微积分课程，主要面向具备基础微积分和线性代数知识的本科生。课程内容涵盖将微分微积分扩展到更一般的向量空间函数，包括输入为矩阵并返回矩阵逆或因式分解的函数、常微分方程解的导数，以及随机函数的导数。课程强调实际计算应用，如大规模优化和机器学习，需重新构思导数计算以应对复杂计算。此外，课程还讨论了效率问题，介绍了“伴随”或“反向模式”微分（即“反向传播”），并简要介绍了现代自动微分技术。这些讲义基于2023年1月的MIT短期课程18.063 "Matrix Calculus"。

补充讨论：

Abstract:
This course, intended for undergraduates familiar with elementary calculus and linear algebra, introduces the extension of differential calculus to functions on more general vector spaces, such as functions that take as input a matrix and return a matrix inverse or factorization, derivatives of ODE solutions, and even stochastic derivatives of random functions. It emphasizes practical computational applications, such as large-scale optimization and machine learning, where derivatives must be re-imagined in order to be propagated through complicated calculations. The class also discusses efficiency concerns leading to "adjoint" or "reverse-mode" differentiation (a.k.a. "backpropagation"), and gives a gentle introduction to modern automatic differentiation (AD) techniques.

data.title: Lvgl: Embedded graphics library to create beautiful UIs
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: LVGL（Light and Versatile Graphics Library）是一个成熟、开源的嵌入式图形库，用于为各种微控制器（MCU）、微处理器（MPU）和显示类型创建美观的用户界面（UI）。它获得了Arm、STM32、NXP、Arduino等知名厂商的支持，具有丰富的功能，包括30+内置控件、强大的样式系统、类似Flexbox和Grid的布局引擎，以及支持多语言的排版系统。LVGL仅需32kB RAM和128kB Flash，兼容多种显示设备，并可在多种操作系统下运行。它基于MIT许可，适用于商业项目，提供MicroPython和PikaScript绑定，支持Make和CMake构建系统，并允许在PC上开发并移植到嵌入式设备。LVGL团队还提供UI设计和咨询服务，用户可通过GitHub Sponsors进行捐赠以支持其发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Embedded graphics library"（嵌入式图形库）的适用性、功能、以及与其他工具的比较和使用体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• [jeremyjh] 认为"Embedded graphics library"并不模糊，对其他用户讨论网页UI、GPU等问题感到困惑，认为偏离了主题。
• [whitehexagon] 分享了自己使用LVGL（8.3.3）结合Zig/WASM/PinePhone的经验，强调LVGL的简洁性以及通过简单帧缓冲方法实现UI的优势，并提到在WASM环境下进行UI开发可以加快迭代，无需频繁部署到手机硬件上。此外，对LVGL团队的文档和示例表示赞赏。
• [androiddrew] 提到LVGL可以与Micropython一起使用，但建议使用第三方移植版本，而不是官方版本，并指出该第三方版本在处理自定义字体和API问题上的优势。
• [nabilt] 推荐了NXP的GUI Glider工具，作为不希望为官方工具付费的替代方案。
• [karmicthreat] 认为LVGL适合构建简单的嵌入式UI，但指出在特定平台上开始时可能有些困难，不过一旦运行起来就很顺利。同时，对编辑器不是VSCode插件表示遗憾。
• [amelius] 对LVGL如何与屏幕交互提出疑问，质疑其无外部依赖的声明。
• [transpute] 分享了一个使用Linux帧缓冲从shell脚本运行LVGL的PoC项目链接。
• [throwaway290] 将LVGL与Dear ImGui进行比较，认为ImGui更小巧且非常适合嵌入式环境，速度极快。
• [kunjanshah] 询问是否有使用LVGL与inkplate EPDs（电子纸显示屏）的经验。
• [einpoklum] 质疑LVGL是否在重复造轮子，指出已经存在多个C语言的GUI库/工具包。
• [ashishb] 寻找一种用于构建纯Web UI的高级库，要求生成小型独立的JavaScript/CSS文件，而不是像React/Vue那样的框架。

补充讨论：
• LVGL的简洁性和易用性受到部分用户（如[whitehexagon]）的好评，尤其是在嵌入式环境中的表现。
• 用户对LVGL与其他工具（如Micropython、Dear ImGui）的比较和选择有不同看法，形成了对不同库优缺点的讨论。
• 部分用户（如[nabilt]和[karmicthreat]）提到了LVGL编辑器的使用体验和与其他工具的集成问题。
• 关于LVGL如何与屏幕交互的技术细节（如[amelius]的提问）以及在不同平台（如WASM和PinePhone）上的实现方式也有一定讨论。
• 争议的焦点可能在于LVGL是否提供了独特的功能，还是仅仅在重复已有工具的功能（[einpoklum]的观点）。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕LVGL的使用体验、技术细节、与其他工具的比较以及在不同平台上的实现方式展开。

📒 Overview
Mature and Well-known
LVGL is the most popular free and open source embedded graphics library to create beautiful UIs for any MCU, MPU and display type. It's supported by industry leading vendors and projects like  Arm, STM32, NXP, Espressif, Nuvoton, Arduino, RT-Thread, Zephyr, NuttX, Adafruit and many more.
Feature Rich
It has all the features to create modern and beautiful GUIs: 30+ built-in widgets, a powerful style system, web inspired layout managers, and a typography system supporting many languages. To integrate LVGL into your platform, all you need is at least 32kB RAM and 128 kB Flash, a C compiler, a frame buffer, and at least an 1/10 screen sized buffer for rendering.
Services
Our team is ready to help you with graphics design, UI implementation and consulting services. Contact us if you need some support during the development of your next GUI project.
🚀 Features
Free and Portable
A fully portable C (C++ compatible) library with no external dependencies.
Can be compiled to any MCU or MPU, with any (RT)OS.
Supports monochrome, ePaper, OLED or TFT displays, or even monitors.
Displays
Distributed under the MIT license, so you can easily use it in commercial projects too.
Needs only 32kB RAM and 128 kB Flash, a frame buffer, and at least an 1/10 screen sized buffer for rendering.
OS, External memory and GPU are supported but not required.
Widgets, Styles, Layouts and more
30+ built-in
Widgets
:  Button, Label, Slider, Chart, Keyboard, Meter, Arc, Table and many more.
Flexible
Style system
with  ~100 style properties to customize any part of the widgets in any state.
Flexbox
and
Grid
-like layouts engines to automatically size and position the widgets in a responsive way.
Texts are rendered with UTF-8 encoding supporting CJK, Thai, Hindi, Arabic, Persian writing systems.
Word wrapping, kerning, text scrolling, sub-pixel rendering, Pinyin-IME Chinese input, Emojis in texts.
Rendering engine supporting animations, anti-aliasing, opacity, smooth scrolling, shadows, image transformation, etc
Supports Mouse, Touchpad, Keypad, Keyboard, External buttons, Encoder

support.

• [whitehexagon] 分享了自己使用LVGL（8.3.3）结合Zig/WASM/PinePhone的经验，强调LVGL的简洁性以及通过简单帧缓冲方法实现UI的优势，并提到在WASM环境下进行UI开发可以加快迭代，无需频繁部署到手机硬件上。此外，对LVGL团队的文档和示例表示赞赏。
• [androiddrew] 提到LVGL可以与Micropython一起使用，但建议使用第三方移植版本，而不是官方版本，并指出该第三方版本在处理自定义字体和API问题上的优势。
• [nabilt] 推荐了NXP的GUI Glider工具，作为不希望为官方工具付费的替代方案。
• [karmicthreat] 认为LVGL适合构建简单的嵌入式UI，但指出在特定平台上开始时可能有些困难，不过一旦运行起来就很顺利。同时，对编辑器不是VSCode插件表示遗憾。
• [amelius] 对LVGL如何与屏幕交互提出疑问，质疑其无外部依赖的声明。
• [transpute] 分享了一个使用Linux帧缓冲从shell脚本运行LVGL的PoC项目链接。
• [throwaway290] 将LVGL与Dear ImGui进行比较，认为ImGui更小巧且非常适合嵌入式环境，速度极快。
• [kunjanshah] 询问是否有使用LVGL与inkplate EPDs（电子纸显示屏）的经验。
• [einpoklum] 质疑LVGL是否在重复造轮子，指出已经存在多个C语言的GUI库/工具包。
• [ashishb] 寻找一种用于构建纯Web UI的高级库，要求生成小型独立的JavaScript/CSS文件，而不是像React/Vue那样的框架。

补充讨论：
• LVGL的简洁性和易用性受到部分用户（如[whitehexagon]）的好评，尤其是在嵌入式环境中的表现。
• 用户对LVGL与其他工具（如Micropython、Dear ImGui）的比较和选择有不同看法，形成了对不同库优缺点的讨论。
• 部分用户（如[nabilt]和[karmicthreat]）提到了LVGL编辑器的使用体验和与其他工具的集成问题。
• 关于LVGL如何与屏幕交互的技术细节（如[amelius]的提问）以及在不同平台（如WASM和PinePhone）上的实现方式也有一定讨论。
• 争议的焦点可能在于LVGL是否提供了独特的功能，还是仅仅在重复已有工具的功能（[einpoklum]的观点）。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕LVGL的使用体验、技术细节、与其他工具的比较以及在不同平台上的实现方式展开。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容的版权问题及其实际应用

不同观点：
• [rustc] 认为AI无法判断其输出是否与训练材料有足够差异，即使输出内容与现有内容匹配，AI公司提供的使用许可可能无法保护用户。

• [bionhoward] 提到OpenAI的用户协议中包含了客户不得与OpenAI竞争的条款。

• [6stringmerc] 强调在美国AI生成内容目前不符合版权保护资格，即使有人主张版权保护，这在法律上也是不成立的。

补充讨论：
• [knewter] 提到发现了一个网站"FreeOutput"，用于比较不同AI供应商是否将版权分配给用户。
• [IshKebab] 原本期待有工具能够检查AI输出是否匹配任何版权材料，认为这样的功能才真正有用。

争议焦点：
- AI生成内容的版权归属问题及其法律保护可行性。
- AI公司提供的用户协议条款是否限制了用户的实际使用自由，尤其是竞争限制条款。

data.title: OSS-SEC: Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary:
Qualys 安全咨询报告披露了 Ubuntu 未授权用户命名空间限制的三个绕过方法。Ubuntu 23.10 引入了这些限制，并在 24.04 版本中默认启用，旨在减少内核攻击面。然而，研究人员发现了三种绕过方法，使本地攻击者可以在命名空间内获得管理员权限，从而利用内核漏洞：

1. 通过 `aa-exec` 工具切换到允许创建命名空间的 AppArmor 配置文件。
2. 通过执行默认安装的 `busybox` shell，利用其配置文件的权限。
3. 通过 `LD_PRELOAD` 预加载到一个允许创建命名空间的程序中。

这些绕过方法仅在命名空间内有效，不会影响主机系统。Ubuntu 已发布相关信息，进一步说明可参考其官方讨论帖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux安全机制中的AppArmor配置文件和用户命名空间是否构成安全漏洞

不同观点：
• [o11c] 认为这并不是一个直接的漏洞，需要已经拥有内核`CAP_SYS_ADMIN`权限才能执行恶意操作。同时指出，许多安全工具在处理多进程解释器时表现不佳，但未详细展开。

• [eqvinox] 认为这是安全层面的失败，即使这个漏洞本身不太大，但仍然不理想。特别是如果用户依赖这些安全特性，而出现这种漏洞会破坏这种信任。尽管承认问题不大，但仍然认为这种安全断裂不可忽视。

• [mjevans] 提出疑问，认为如果没有AppArmor的额外"祝福"，标准的Linux权限和容器组是否足以防止这种特权环境逃逸。这暗示了对AppArmor有效性的质疑，并关注标准Linux安全机制的作用。

• [quotemstr] 强烈反对将未授权的用户命名空间视作安全漏洞，批评Ubuntu禁用这些命名空间的决定是短视的。认为移除这些功能会让良好行为的程序更难设置用户空间沙箱，主张修复内核漏洞而不是随意破坏有用特性。

• [j45] 关注该问题的影响范围，询问这到底是仅限于Ubuntu的问题，还是Debian等其他Linux发行版也可能受到影响，显示出对问题普遍性的关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于未授权的用户命名空间和AppArmor配置文件是否构成安全漏洞，以及Ubuntu禁用用户命名空间的决定是否合理。
• 讨论还涉及标准Linux权限和容器技术在防止特权环境逃逸中的作用，以及内核漏洞与安全机制之间的关系。
• 不同评论者对安全断裂的容忍度和对安全工具的期望也存在分歧，部分认为这是小问题，部分则认为影响较大。

43517734.article_content:
oss-sec
mailing list archives
By Date
By Thread
Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
From
: Qualys Security Advisory <qsa () qualys com>
Date
: Thu, 27 Mar 2025 17:44:15 +0000
Qualys Security Advisory
Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
========================================================================
Contents
========================================================================
Summary
Bypass via aa-exec
Bypass via busybox
Bypass via LD_PRELOAD
Acknowledgments
Timeline (advisory sent to the Ubuntu Security Team on January 15, 2025)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Prologue, from
https://grsecurity.net/10_years_of_linux_security.pdf:
+ February 2013 (v3.8) - Unprivileged User Namespace support added
- Greatly increased kernel attack surface, exposed many interfaces
that previously saw little security scrutiny
+ Attack surface exposed by unprivileged user namespaces isn't
decreasing anytime soon
- Even more functionality being exposed
------------------------------------------------------------------------
========================================================================
Summary
========================================================================
Ubuntu 23.10 introduced unprivileged user namespace restrictions (the
sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns) and Ubuntu 24.04
enabled them by default. From Alex Murray's excellent blog post at
https://ubuntu.com/blog/whats-new-in-security-for-ubuntu-24-04-lts:
"Unprivileged user namespaces are a widely used feature of the Linux
kernel, providing additional security isolation for applications, and
are often employed as part of a sandbox environment. However, [...]
unprivileged user namespaces also expose additional attack surfaces
within the Linux kernel. There has been a long history of (ab)use of
unprivileged user namespaces to exploit various kernel
vulnerabilities.
For Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, the use of unprivileged user namespaces is then
allowed for all applications but access to any additional permissions
within the namespace are denied. This allows more applications to more
gracefully handle this default restriction whilst still protecting
against the abuse of user namespaces to gain access to additional
attack surfaces within the Linux kernel."
Unfortunately, we discovered three different bypasses of these
unprivileged user namespace restrictions; each bypass allows a local
attacker to create user namespaces with full administrator capabilities,
and therefore to still exploit vulnerabilities in kernel components that
require capabilities such as CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_ADMIN:
- An unprivileged local attacker can simply use the aa-exec tool (which
is installed by default on Ubuntu) to transition to one of the many
pre-configured AppArmor profiles that do allow the creation of user
namespaces with full capabilities (for example, the chrome, flatpak,
or trinity profile).
- An unprivileged local attacker can first execute a busybox shell,
which is installed by default on Ubuntu, and is one of the programs
whose pre-configured AppArmor profile does allow the creation of user
namespaces with full capabilities.
- An unprivileged local attacker can LD_PRELOAD a shell into one of the
programs whose pre-configured AppArmor profile does allow the creation
of user namespaces with full capabilities (for example, nautilus is
installed by default on Ubuntu Desktop).
Clarification: such a bypass allows an unprivileged user to obtain full
capabilities *inside* a namespace, not on the host outside a namespace;
for comparison, a bypass is not even needed on most Linux distributions,
because they allow unprivileged users to obtain full capabilities inside
namespaces by default (and therefore to exploit CAP_SYS_ADMIN kernel
vulnerabilities for example), without any restriction at all.
For more information on these bypasses and user namespace restrictions,
please refer to Ubuntu's post at:
https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/understanding-apparmor-user-namespace-restriction
========================================================================
Bypass via aa-exec
========================================================================
Are we all just algorithms doing what we're supposed to do or can we
escape our programming?
-- Jude, The Matrix Resurrections
While working on needrestart, particularly on commit e17b564 ("core: fix
regression of false positives for processes running in chroot or mountns
(#317)"), we tried to experiment with user and mount namespaces, but to
our great surprise we were barred from creating them as an unprivileged
user on Ubuntu 24.04 (although kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone is
enabled by default):
------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ id
uid=1001(tiffany) gid=1001(tiffany) groups=1001(tiffany),100(users)
$ unshare -U -r -m /bin/sh
unshare: write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation no

data.title: The disappearance of Gaia, ESA spacecraft will be turned off on 27 March 2025
data.author: croes
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了欧空局（ESA）盖亚 spacecraft的任务结束及其后续数据发布计划。盖亚自2013年发射以来，一直在太空中绘制数十亿颗恒星的位置和运动，预计将于2025年3月27日停止运行并进行钝化处理。尽管航天器即将退役，但盖亚任务仍在继续，未来将发布两个主要数据集：2026年的数据发布4（DR4）和2030年的数据发布5（DR5）。此外，文章还提及了与盖亚数据处理相关的一个博士后职位招聘信息，以及3月4日盖亚最后一次被地面望远镜观测到的事件。盖亚的科学贡献将在未来几年继续通过数据处理和分析联盟（DPAC）的工作延续下去。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gaia卫星的任务结束及其相关技术与社会影响

不同观点：
• [margalabargala] 指出，Gaia卫星被移至“墓地轨道”是因为燃料耗尽，且L2拉格朗日点是有限且宝贵的空间资源，不能让报废卫星占用。在墓地轨道上，Gaia无法继续执行其科学任务。
• [sega_sai] 补充说明，在关闭卫星之前，他们还重写了卫星计算机的EEPROM，因为担心卫星会重新启动。这表明卫星具有多种自主恢复模式，存在重新激活的可能。
• [ISL] 表达了对参与Gaia任务的人员及为任务做出贡献的人（包括纳税人）的感谢，认为Gaia的数据将对未来几代人对宇宙的理解产生深远影响。
• [bhouston] 分享了Gaia项目的一些图片链接，引导人们关注项目取得的视觉成果。
• [TMEHpodcast] 从历史角度评论了Gaia使用的三角测量法（视差法），指出该方法自古以来被用于导航，如今被用于绘制星系地图，强调了几何学在探索未知中的持续重要性。
• [pfdietz] 对将机器赋予人类情感（如“享受退休”）的做法提出批评，认为不应将情感投射到机器上。

补充讨论：
• [catlikesshrimp] 提出了关于将卫星留在轨道上而不是让其坠入海洋的问题，认为坠入海洋可能存在风险，因为卫星可能在未来坠落到重要设施或城市上，造成更大范围的损害。这一观点引发了对空间垃圾和卫星退役处理方式的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于卫星退役处理的技术选择和伦理问题，比如是否应让卫星留在轨道上，还是选择让其坠入海洋，以及是否可以对机器进行拟人化描述。

Gaia Mission News - Gaia
Gaia News
2025-03-21
The disappearance of Gaia
On 4 March, astronomer Zhuo-Xiao Wang captured this view of the sudden disappearance of ESA’s Gaia spacecraft. After more than 11 years in space mapping the motions and properties of billions of stars, the spacecraft’s operations are coming to an end. Gaia will be switched off on 27 March 2025. During a series of final test operations, flight controllers at ESA’s ESOC mission control centre rotated Gaia, causing its sunshield to reflect more light towards Earth. As a result, Gaia appeared much brighter than usual and was observed by several citizen astronomers around the world. Gaia is seen here moving across the sky, initially brightening before vanishing as the spacecraft quickly rotates back to its typical orientation. This was the final time that Gaia will appear so bright to astronomers on Earth. The spacecraft will now remain ‘dark’ forever. The Gaia mission, however, will continue and culminate in two major data releases that are in preparation for 2026 and 2030.

data.title: Vramfs: Vram Based Filesystem for Linux
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary:
**vramfs** 是一个基于 Linux 的文件系统工具，利用 FUSE 库将文件系统创建于显卡的显存（VRAM）中，类似于内存盘（ramdisk），但使用的是显卡的显存。该工具并非为严肃场景设计，但在消费级 GPU（显存 4GB 以上）上表现良好。读写性能分别约为 2.4 GB/s 和 2.0 GB/s，约为内存盘的三分之一。

**要求**：
- Linux 内核 2.6+
- FUSE 开发文件
- 支持 OpenCL 1.2 的显卡

**构建**：
安装 OpenCL 驱动并确认显卡被识别，安装 `libfuse3-dev` 及其他必要文件，运行 `make` 构建。

**挂载**：
使用 `bin/vramfs <mountdir> <size>` 挂载，建议大小不超过 VRAM 的 50% 以避免不稳定。

**实现**：
vramfs 通过 FUSE 库实现用户空间文件系统，使用 OpenCL 分配显存，支持异步写入和同步读取，文件系统结构为树状目录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA CUDA Direct Storage技术及其相关方案的优缺点，特别是在利用GPU和VRAM作为文件系统存储方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持使用CUDA Direct Storage**：[fp64]提到NVIDIA CUDA Direct Storage提供了一种高效的文件传输方式，连接GPU和本地文件系统，表示有兴趣尝试。
• **内核模块方案**：[devit]认为更好的方案是编写Linux内核模块，通过DRM保留GPU RAM来创建ramdisks，而不是使用OpenCL创建用户空间文件系统。该方案强调了更好的缓存机制和并发文件系统支持。
• **质疑速度**：[shadowpho]认为2 GB/s的速度较慢，指出DDR5内存应达到6 GB/s以上的速度。
• **利用RAM/VRAM作为文件系统的实用性**：[harha_]支持利用RAM和VRAM作为文件系统，认为在某些情况下不需要纯RAM/VRAM。
• **对使用VRAM存储文件的幽默态度**：[finnjohnsen2]以幽默的口吻评论使用宝贵的VRAM来存储文件，表示对其实现感到意外。

补充讨论：
• **FUSE文件系统的开销及优化**：[12destroyer21]询问FUSE文件系统相对于内核实现的开销，并提出是否可以使用eBPF来加速FUSE类似的文件系统驱动。
• **硬件选择问题**：[hinkley]讨论了使用旧显卡还是PCIe NVMe多路复用器的性价比问题。
• **能耗问题**：[Dwedit]指出使用这种方案会使GPU持续供电，无法自行关闭。
• **其他硬件方案**：[dheera]不支持使用GPU VRAM，认为CPU与GPU的复制速度不佳，建议直接使用大容量的CPU VRAM。
• **其他技术联想**：[ggm]提到树莓派的图形处理器可以作为引导加载器，[knome]建议将VRAM用作类似zram的交换文件存储。

争议焦点：
• **方案选择的争议**：内核模块方案与CUDA Direct Storage用户空间方案的优劣对比，特别是在缓存和并发支持方面的讨论。
• **速度和效率的争议**：对2 GB/s速度的质疑，以及对DDR5内存预期速度的讨论。
• **使用VRAM存储文件的实用性和合理性**：一部分评论者认为使用VRAM存储文件不切实际或效率低下，另一部分评论者则认为在特定情况下有其实用价值。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **技术实现细节**：包括FUSE开销、能耗管理、以及不同硬件配置下的性能对比。
• **替代方案的提出**：如使用zram或直接使用CPU VRAM的建议。

vramfs
Unused RAM is wasted RAM, so why not put some of that VRAM in your graphics card
to work?
vramfs is a utility that uses the
FUSE library
to create a file system in VRAM. The idea is pretty much the same as a ramdisk,
except that it uses the video RAM of a discrete graphics card to store
files. It is not intented for serious use, but it does actually work fairly
well, especially since consumer GPUs with 4GB or more VRAM are now available.
On the developer's system, the continuous read performance is ~2.4 GB/s and
write performance 2.0 GB/s, which is about 1/3 of what is achievable with a
ramdisk. That is already decent enough for a device not designed for large data
transfers to the host, but future development should aim to get closer to the
PCI-e bandwidth limits. See the
benchmarks
section for more info.
Requirements
Linux with kernel 2.6+
FUSE development files
A graphics card with support for OpenCL 1.2
Building
First, install the OpenCL driver for your graphics card and verify that it's
recognized as an OpenCL device by running
clinfo
. Then install the
libfuse3-dev
package or build it from source. You will also need
pkg-config
and OpenCL
development files, (
opencl-dev
,
opencl-clhpp-headers
package or equivalent),
with version 1.2 of the OpenCL headers at least.
Just run
make
to build
vramfs
.
If you want to debug with valgrind, you should compile with the minimal fake
OpenCL implementation to avoid filling your screen with warnings caused by the
OpenCL driver:
valgrind:
make DEBUG=1
Mounting
Mount a disk by running
bin/vramfs <mountdir> <size>
. The
mountdir
can be
any empty directory. The
size
is the disk size in bytes. For more information,
run
bin/vramfs
without arguments.
The recommended maximum size of a vramdisk is 50% of your VRAM. If you go over
that, your driver or system may become unstable because it has to start
swapping. For example, webpages in Chrome will stop rendering properly.
If the disk has been inactive for a while, the graphics card will likely lower
its memory clock, which means it'll take a second to get up to speed again.
Implementation
The FUSE library is used to implement vramfs as a user space file system. This
eases development and makes working with APIs such as OpenCL straightforward.
Basic architecture
When the program is started, it checks for an OpenCL capable GPU and attempts to
allocate the specified amount of memory. Once the memory has been allocated, the
root entry object is created and a global reference to it is stored.
FUSE then forwards calls like
stat
,
readdir
and
write
to the file system
functions. These will then locate the entry through the root entry using the
specified path. The required operations will then be performed on the entry
object. If the entry is a file object, the operation may lead to OpenCL
cvEnqueueReadBuffer
or
cvEnqueueWriteBuffer
calls to manipulate the data.
When a file is created or opened, a
file_session
object is created to store
the reference to the file object and any other data that is persistent between
an
fopen
and
fclose
call.
VRAM block allocation
OpenCL is used to allocate blocks of memory on the graphics card by creating
buffer objects. When a new disk is mounted, a pool of
disk size / block size
buffers is created and initialised with zeros. That is not just a good practice,
but it's also required with some OpenCL drivers to check if the VRAM required
for the block is actually available. Unfortunately Nvidia cards don't support
OpenCL 1.2, which means the
cvEnqueueFillBuffer
call has to be simulated by
copying from a preallocated buffer filled with zeros. Somewhat interestingly, it
doesn't seem to make a difference in performance on cards that support both.
Writes to blocks are generally asynchronous, whereas reads are synchronous.
Luckily, OpenCL guarantees in-order execution of commands by default, which
means reads of a block will wait for the writes to complete. OpenCL 1.1 is
completely thread safe, so no special care is required when sending commands.
Block objects are managed using a
shared_ptr
so that they can automatically
reinsert themselves into the pool on deconstruction.
File system
The file system is a tree of
entry_t
objects with members for attributes like
the parent directory, mode and access time. Each type of entry has its own
subclass that derives from it:
file_t
,
dir_t
and
symlink_t
. The main file
that implements all of the FUSE ca

data.title: Beautiful and Minimalistic Chrome Extension
data.author: reynnan
data.article_summary: Lofi Tab是一款浏览器扩展，旨在将新标签页转变为高效且宁静的体验。它提供待办事项管理、可自定义的时钟、实时天气信息以及超过30种精美的Lofi背景供选择。该扩展轻量优化，仅800kb，不会拖慢浏览器速度。用户可以通过添加至Chrome或Edge浏览器来享受这些功能，并提高新标签页的实用性和美观度。Lofi Tab获得了4.8分的高评分，已有1,000多名用户使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome扩展的功能、设计美学、版权问题以及用户定制化需求

不同观点：
• [ahmedfromtunis] 认为Chrome扩展的功能性比美观更重要，他更喜欢能够替代新标签页并具备笔记功能的扩展，比如因与V3 manifest不兼容而无法使用的Papier。
• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 仅简单评价为“极简主义”，未展开具体观点。
• [rendaw] 关注背景图片的版权问题，指出“来源”链接指向一个未注明出处的Tumblr页面。
• [AlexanderTheGr8] 提到自己也在制作类似的新标签页扩展，并认为Chrome应提供更多内置的定制化选项，如问候语、日历和任务整合。
• [williamscales] 幽默地指出，最极简的新标签页其实是空白页，同时对该扩展的简洁设计表示赞赏。
• [piokoch] 担心该扩展使用的吉卜力工作室电影图像和片段可能违反了合理使用规则。
• [wffurr] 质疑动画背景的“ calming（平静）”效果，认为动画可能并不符合所有人对平静的理解。
• [modzu] 询问该扩展是否开源，并推荐了一个带有书签功能的新标签页扩展。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及的版权问题和合理使用规则成为一个值得注意的法律和道德讨论点。
• 用户对Chrome新标签页的定制化需求明显，尤其是对集成更多实用功能（如日历、任务）的期望较高。
• 不同用户对“极简主义”和“美观”的理解存在差异，有人看重功能性，有人则在意设计美学。

• [AlexanderTheGr8] 提到自己也在制作类似的新标签页扩展，并认为Chrome应提供更多内置的定制化选项，如问候语、日历和任务整合。
• [williamscales] 幽默地指出，最极简的新标签页其实是空白页，同时对该扩展的简洁设计表示赞赏。
• [piokoch] 担心该扩展使用的吉卜力工作室电影图像和片段可能违反了合理使用规则。
• [wffurr] 质疑动画背景的“ calming（平静）”效果，认为动画可能并不符合所有人对平静的理解。
• [modzu] 询问该扩展是否开源，并推荐了一个带有书签功能的新标签页扩展。

• 评论中涉及的版权问题和合理使用规则成为一个值得注意的法律和道德讨论点。

data.article_summary: 文章指出，随着无现金社会的兴起，英国儿童因吞咽异物而需要接受手术的病例显著减少。根据英格兰皇家外科医学院的数据，2012年至2022年间，此类手术数量下降了29%。历史上，硬币占六岁以下儿童吞咽异物的75%以上，而无现金支付的普及减少了家中的硬币数量，从而降低了相关手术的需求。尽管病例减少，医生仍提醒家长警惕纽扣电池和磁铁等危险物品。NHS数据显示，这种趋势不仅有益于儿童安全，也缓解了医疗系统的压力。

43518251.article_content:
Historically, coins accounted for more than 75% of objects swallowed by children under six, the Royal College of Surgeons of England said.
Photograph: fStop Images GmbH/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
Historically, coins accounted for more than 75% of objects swallowed by children under six, the Royal College of Surgeons of England said.
Photograph: fStop Images GmbH/Alamy
Children
Decline of cash credited for drop in NHS surgery for children swallowing objects
Figures reveal 29% fall in operations in England to remove foreign bodies from children’s airways, noses and throats
Denis Campbell
Health policy editor
Thu 27 Mar 2025 20.01 EDT
Share
Cashless societies may be a sad fact of modern life for those with a nostalgic attachment to the pound in their pocket, but doctors have discovered one unexpected benefit of the decline of coins.
Far fewer children are having surgery after swallowing small items that could choke or kill them, and the scarcity of loose change is likely to be the reason.
The number of children in
England
needing an operation to remove a foreign body from their nose, throat or airway fell significantly between 2012 and 2022, NHS figures show.
The fall has been greeted with relief by doctors and surgeons, who for years have been warning of the dangers posed by young children ingesting magnets, tiny batteries and other risky objects.
How Covid changed children in Britain
Read more
The number of under-18s undergoing surgery on their nose, airway or throat for that reason has declined from 2,405 in 2012 to 1,716 in 2022 – a fall of 29% or 689 cases in the year.
The Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCSE), which obtained the figures, collated from hospital admission data, identified the rise of the cashless society as the main reason.
“Historically, coins accounted for over 75% of objects swallowed by children under six years old, and fewer coins in homes due to contactless payments have likely helped reduce the number of these procedures,” it said.
For example, surgeons performed 484 (31%) fewer procedures to remove something from a child’s nose in 2022 compared with 2012. There were 28% fewer on the digestive tract in the same age group and 8% fewer involving their airways.
However, the RCSE said that, despite the drop, parents should still be alert to the risk of their child swallowing shiny objects that looked like coins, such as button batteries and magnets.
“These can cause deadly internal complications within hours of ingestion, leading to tragic consequences,” it added.
This week,
reports
told how one-year-old Araya Whateley had to have her bowel removed after ingesting six metal balls from a toy belonging to her nine-year-old sister.

Parents who suspect their child may have ingested something dangerous should take them straight to hospital to get checked out, according to the body that represents Britain’s A&E doctors.
“If any carer thinks a child has swallowed an item they shouldn’t have, take them to A&E – even if they have no symptoms. In cases like this, it really is better to be safe than sorry,” said Dr Adrian Boyle, the president of the Royal College of Emergency Medicine.
“As a parent, I know we all do our best to be vigilant as to what our children are putting in their mouths. But it is impossible to monitor them all the time.”
Prof Stephen Powis,
NHS
England’s national medical director, said: “At a time when demand on NHS services is so high, trends like this one which reduces hospital attendances is not only good for children, but also for our under-pressure staff.”

data.title: The Wrong Way to Use a Signed Distance Function (SDF)
data.author: AnthonBerg
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了使用有向距离函数（signed distance functions, SDFs）进行粒子与几何体碰撞检测的方法。通常，SDF用于光线追踪和着色器中以定义无网格几何体，但文章探讨了一种“非传统”用法：生成点云几何体。通过计算粒子与球体中心的距离，判断粒子是否与球体相撞。若距离小于球体半径，则粒子在球体内，否则在外部或表面。文章还提到，通过重新定义距离函数，可以扩展至检测与多个几何体（如盒子、环面等）的碰撞。SDF的优势在于其可替换性和组合性，使得碰撞检测更加直观和灵活。

43517365.article_content:
Disclaimer: there’s nothing wrong with using a sdf this way.
Recently, my good friend Mike Brondbjerg posted this on Twitter:
Dark Matter: 50,000 particles passing through a field until they hit a hidden sphere. By varying the distance travelled each step, the collisions are more / less accurate, so creating a nice fuzziness around the spheres.
#generative
#design
#creativecommuting
#creativecoding
pic.twitter.com/gmFEV7fCwk
— Mike Brondbjerg (@mikebrondbjerg)
January 15, 2020
You can follow along and see how this idea is evolving into the beautiful, elegant line drawings that are the hallmark of his style.
Dark Matter: random walk obstacle avoidance… nice random output.
#creativecoding
#generative
#design
#processing
pic.twitter.com/DTzy7H2G6Z
— Mike Brondbjerg (@mikebrondbjerg)
January 26, 2020
Spheres
Mike’s post gave me an idea, a way to introduce a concept I like to use in some of my work: signed distance functions. Sdfs are more commonly associated with raytracing and shaders, and by far the best source to learn about them in that context is Inigo Quilez, of
Shadertoy
fame:
https://iquilezles.org/
.
But there is a delightfully wrong way to use a sdf. Their primary use in raytracing and shaders is to define meshless geometry. For example, a way to draw smooth spheres without generating a ton of triangles. The use I’m showing here is the exact opposite: to generate geometry, point clouds in fact. Geometry that then needs to be processed in a conventional way before it can be rendered on the screen.
Let’s imagine we want to tackle something similar to the tweet: particles colliding with a sphere. One way to do this is by calculating the distance of the particle to the center of the sphere, let’s keep it at the origin. For a particle
\vec{p}
at position
(x,y,z)
, this distance is given by:
{d( \vec{p} )=\sqrt{x.x+y.y+z.z}}
. If that distance
d
is larger than the radius
r
of the sphere, the particle is outside the sphere, if it’s smaller then it is inside, if it’s exactly the same then it is on the surface.
\begin{cases}  d( \vec{p} )<r, & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is inside} \\  d( \vec{p} )=r , & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is on sphere}\\  d( \vec{p} )>r, & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is outside}  \end{cases}
Using this, we can check the particles every step. As long as their distance to the sphere is larger than the radius, they’re fine. If a particle takes a step and its distance becomes smaller or equal, it has hit the sphere.
A grid of particles flying into a sphere. Some have collided with the sphere, the rest is zooming off into infinity.
If the sphere is not in the origin but centered in a point
\vec{c} (cx,cy,cz)
the distance function becomes
{d( \vec{p} , \vec{c} )=\sqrt{(x-cx).(x-cx)+(y-cy).(y-cy)+(z-cz).(z-cz)}}
. Typically, this is explained as the length of the vector going from
\vec{p}
to
\vec{c}
. Another way to see it, that will serve us well further on, is to imagine that we shift the sphere to the origin,
\vec{c}\to\vec{0}
, and the entire space moves with it . Our particle is then moved
\vec{p}\to\vec{p}-\vec{c}
. Checking a particle at
\vec{p}
against a sphere in center
\vec{c}
is the same as doing it for a particle at
\vec{p}-\vec{c}
against a sphere in the origin.
Since we can put the sphere wherever we want, we can add multiple spheres. Each particle is then tested against the different spheres one by one.
A grid of particles flying into a bunch of spheres.
Distance Fields
In creative coding, it is often useful to have several perspectives to look at things. The equations above can be refactored:
\begin{cases}  d( \vec{p} )-r<0, & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is inside} \\  d( \vec{p} )-r=0 , & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is on sphere}\\  d( \vec{p} )-r>0, & \text{if }  \vec{p}\text{ is outside}  \end{cases}
Nothing has really changed, the equations are still the same. But what they describe is a function
{d( \vec{p} )-r}
that separates space in three regions: one region outside the sphere, with positive values; one region inside the sphere, with negative values; and the surface of the sphere itself, where the function equals zero. This is the signed distance function of a sphere in the origin, with radius
r
.
Testing the particles at each step is essentially the same evaluation: calculate the function at
\vec{p}
and see how it classifies. The advantage of seeing it this way is that the signed distance function can be easily replaced, and suddenly we’re checking collisions with a box, a torus, or any of the many shapes that have a well-defined sdf, like
the list
Inigo keeps.
A grid of particles flying into a bunch of boxes.
In itself, there’s nothing stopping us from using the first approach to calculate the distance of a point to some specific geometry. But I find sdfs make it more intuitive, especially when we start modifying and combining them.
Not every function is a signed distance function, there are certain requirements. I’m not going into the rigorous math details, mainly because I

data.title: Body Doubling
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: **身体双人法**（Body Doubling）是一种通过与另一人共同 presence 来帮助完成任务的策略，常用于家务、写作或计算机工作等任务。该方法可以通过物理 presence、电话、视频或社交媒体实现，旨在通过共享目标提高任务完成率。对一些人是共同做类似任务效果最佳，而对另一些人只需在同一空间即可。此方法尤其受到注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）患者的欢迎，用于管理症状和减少分心。虽然长期研究不足，但专家认为该策略通过“外部化动机”帮助ADHD患者提高专注力和生产力。身体双人仅作为支持系统，不参与任务，主要通过减少干扰帮助患者保持专注。该方法也被视为传统ADHD治疗（如药物）的替代或补充方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：身体加倍（body doubling）作为一种提高生产力的策略，其效果和适用场景。

不同观点：
• **支持身体加倍，认为其有效**：
   - [eraviloi] 认为身体加倍有助于消除不完成工作的借口，特别是在复杂任务中，两个人的思维碰撞能提高效率。
   - [nicbou] 通过每周与朋友进行身体加倍会议，结合番茄工作法，认为这种方法既有趣又有效，并计划将此方法与社交活动结合。
   - [grepLeigh] 也支持身体加倍，认为这是安静的陪伴，适合完成一些不需要深度专注的任务，如报税或预订旅行。

• **质疑身体加倍的效果**：
   - [bravetraveler] 认为身体加倍可能带来分心，而不是帮助集中注意力，个人并不觉得被注视能带来安慰。

• **比较与质疑**：
   - [iradik] 质疑身体加倍与监督工作（looking over someone’s shoulder）的区别，认为信任和喜欢的人在旁边会有帮助，但被监督则会降低效率。
   - [teeray] 引用了“痛苦喜欢陪伴”（Misery loves company）的说法，暗示这种策略可能只是因为共同经历不快而有效。

• **将身体加倍与传统办公环境类比**：
   - [TZubiri] 认为这类似于在办公室工作，通过公司的环境自然提高生产力。

• **历史视角与概念重命名**：
   - [javajosh] 认为身体加倍其实就是过去的“同伴压力”（peer pressure），只是现在用了一个新的名称，并用于正向目的。

43517603.article_summary: **身体双人法**（Body Doubling）是一种通过与另一人共同 presence 来帮助完成任务的策略，常用于家务、写作或计算机工作等任务。该方法可以通过物理 presence、电话、视频或社交媒体实现，旨在通过共享目标提高任务完成率。对一些人是共同做类似任务效果最佳，而对另一些人只需在同一空间即可。此方法尤其受到注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）患者的欢迎，用于管理症状和减少分心。虽然长期研究不足，但专家认为该策略通过“外部化动机”帮助ADHD患者提高专注力和生产力。身体双人仅作为支持系统，不参与任务，主要通过减少干扰帮助患者保持专注。该方法也被视为传统ADHD治疗（如药物）的替代或补充方案。

data.title: Utah becomes first US state to ban fluoride in its water
data.author: Jimmc414
data.article_summary: Utah has become the first U.S. state to ban fluoride in its public water supplies, following concerns about potential health risks raised by health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Governor Spencer Cox signed the bill into law, which takes effect on May 7. The ban has faced criticism from public health experts, who argue that fluoride helps prevent cavities and improves oral health, especially for children. Supporters of the ban, like Republican lawmaker Stephanie Gricius, claim it gives citizens a choice regarding fluoride consumption. While most public health organizations support water fluoridation, some recent legal rulings and debates have questioned its necessity, especially given fluoride's availability in toothpaste and other products.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国水氟化问题的不同观点和争议

不同观点：
• [国际视角与非问题化]  
一些评论者如freehorse认为，水氟化是一个美国特有的两极化争论，而世界上其他国家已经解决了这个问题，因此美国应该借鉴其他国家的经验。这种观点认为水氟化在美国是一个被过度讨论的非问题。

• [氟化物的健康影响]  
jiggawatts指出，有研究表明孕期摄入氟化物可能与轻微的智商降低有关，尽管出生后没有显著影响。该评论者建议，移除水中的氟化物并建议孕妇使用不含氟的牙膏，因为现代牙膏和牙医治疗已经足够提供所需的氟化物，继续在水里添加氟化物可能是一种“过度用药”。

• [自由选择与政策]  
efitz认为，由于通过牙膏等途径已经很容易获得足够的氟化物，没有必要强制在水中添加氟化物。在美国，由于牙科护理不属于公共保险覆盖范围，政府没有必要一定在公共水中添加氟化物。应让各地居民自行决定是否氟化水源。

• [地方差异与自然氟化物含量]  
adrr和codybontecou指出，像犹他和夏威夷等地区，有的地方自然含有较高氟化物，甚至不添加氟化物，或者有地方选择不添加氟化物。这显示了美国各地在水氟化问题上的差异和不同做法。

• [历史与阴谋论]  
JKCalhoun以幽默的方式提到了历史上关于水氟化的阴谋论，如将其视为颠覆公共健康的共产主义阴谋，指出这种历史背景可能影响当前的讨论。

• [氟化物的公共健康效应]  
habosa强调了氟化物对口腔健康的连锁效应，认为氟化物不仅影响口腔健康，还可能影响整体健康，如心血管疾病。该评论者批评那些仅因政治得分而反对水氟化的政客，认为他们没有提出替代方案。

• [氟化物双重标准的质疑]  
ryao对氟化物在牙膏和水中的不同使用标准表示质疑，认为这两种使用方式不能共存。

• [氟化物与社会政策]  
fungiblecog指出，如果对含糖饮料征税或让牙科护理变得负担得起，水氟化可能就不必要了，但这种做法在美国往往被视为“共产主义”。

• [智商影响的实证质疑]  
lunarboy以讽刺的方式质疑那些认为氟化物降低智商的人，是否认为夏威夷的孩子智商高于其他州。

补充讨论：
• [过滤氟化物的问题]  
ourmandave提出了关于使用全屋过滤器去除氟化物的实际问题，指出其居住地水质差，但并未涉及氟化物具体问题。

• [历史书籍参考]  
piuantiderp提到了一本由Christopher Bryson撰写的书，暗示需要更多背景知识来理解水氟化争议。

• [最佳证据的请求]  
dataflow请求提供支持水氟化的最佳证据，显示了对讨论中事实基础的需求。

争议焦点：
• 氟化物对健康（特别是智商）的影响以及其必要性。
• 水氟化是否属于过度用药，以及氟化物的替代方案是否足够有效。
• 地方自治与居民自由选择权在水氟化问题上的适用性。
• 政治因素在反对水氟化中的作用。

43517833.article_content:
Utah becomes first US state to ban fluoride in its water
5 hours ago
Share
Save
Nadine Yousif
BBC News
Share
Save
Getty Images
Utah governor Spencer Cox signed the fluoride ban into law this week
Utah has become the first US state to ban the use of fluoride in its public water, following concerns raised by health secretary Robert F Kennedy that the mineral poses potential health risks.
Governor Spencer Cox signed the ban into law this week, which will go into effect on 7 May. Other states, including Florida and Ohio, are weighing similar legislation.
Fluoride has been added to US drinking water since 1945 to prevent cavities.
Utah's move to remove the mineral has been criticised by experts, who worry it will have consequences for oral health, especially for children.
The bill, signed by Cox on Thursday, prohibits communities from adding fluoride to their public water supplies.
The law does not mention any public health concerns related to the mineral, but Republican state lawmaker Stephanie Gricius - who introduced the bill in the state legislature - has argued that there is research suggesting fluoride could have possible cognitive effects in children.
Gricius has said that her bill would give citizens a choice whether they want to consume fluoride or not.
This concern over fluoride was previously raised by Kennedy, the US health secretary, who said in November that "the Trump White House will advise all US water systems to remove fluoride from public water".
He alleged the chemical found in toothpaste and regularly used by dentists "is an industrial waste associated with arthritis, bone fractures, bone cancer, IQ loss, neurodevelopmental disorders, and thyroid disease".
Most public health experts have rejected these claims and alleged that Kennedy had cited data from studies conducted in countries with far higher levels of fluoride in their water systems than the US has.
The American Dental Association sharply criticised Utah for its decision, saying that it shows "wanton disregard for the oral health and well-being of their constituents".
"It is disheartening to see that a proven, public health policy, which exists for the greater good of an entire community's oral health, has been dismantled based on distorted pseudoscience," the association's president, Denver dentist Brett Kessler, said in a statement.
Many public health groups, including the American Academy of Pediatrics and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, have long supported adding small amounts of fluoride to drinking water.
The US Public Health Service reduced the amount of fluoride it recommended adding to water in 2015, but the federal government has encouraged states since the 1960s to add small amounts of the chemical to water to help prevent cavities and aid oral health.
Recent court rulings have led to the reduction of fluoride in US water, and some experts have questioned the continued need for it in water systems given its wide availability in toothpaste and other dental products.
Most of western Europe does not add fluoride to its water. In England, about one in 10 people has fluoridated drinking water, though a programme has since been introduced to fluoridate water for 1.6 million people in north-east England.
By contrast, around 63% of the US population have fluoridated water.
Experts who support putting fluoride in water says studies show that community water fluoridation prevents at least 25% of tooth decay in children and adults.
"The scientific weight of sound evidence around the benefit of community water fluoridation is clear and compelling," the American Dental Association said in October of last year.
Prof Avijit Banerjee, chair of cariology and operative dentistry at King's College London, previously told the BBC that "the potential harmful effects of fluoride cited have not been associated with the very low levels of fluoride used in water fluoridation programmes".

主要讨论点：美国水氟化问题的不同观点和争议

不同观点：
• [国际视角与非问题化]  
一些评论者如freehorse认为，水氟化是一个美国特有的两极化争论，而世界上其他国家已经解决了这个问题，因此美国应该借鉴其他国家的经验。这种观点认为水氟化在美国是一个被过度讨论的非问题。

• [氟化物的健康影响]  
jiggawatts指出，有研究表明孕期摄入氟化物可能与轻微的智商降低有关，尽管出生后没有显著影响。该评论者建议，移除水中的氟化物并建议孕妇使用不含氟的牙膏，因为现代牙膏和牙医治疗已经足够提供所需的氟化物，继续在水里添加氟化物可能是一种“过度用药”。

• [自由选择与政策]  
efitz认为，由于通过牙膏等途径已经很容易获得足够的氟化物，没有必要强制在水中添加氟化物。在美国，由于牙科护理不属于公共保险覆盖范围，政府没有必要一定在公共水中添加氟化物。应让各地居民自行决定是否氟化水源。

• [地方差异与自然氟化物含量]  
adrr和codybontecou指出，像犹他和夏威夷等地区，有的地方自然含有较高氟化物，甚至不添加氟化物，或者有地方选择不添加氟化物。这显示了美国各地在水氟化问题上的差异和不同做法。

• [历史与阴谋论]  
JKCalhoun以幽默的方式提到了历史上关于水氟化的阴谋论，如将其视为颠覆公共健康的共产主义阴谋，指出这种历史背景可能影响当前的讨论。

• [氟化物的公共健康效应]  
habosa强调了氟化物对口腔健康的连锁效应，认为氟化物不仅影响口腔健康，还可能影响整体健康，如心血管疾病。该评论者批评那些仅因政治得分而反对水氟化的政客，认为他们没有提出替代方案。

• [氟化物双重标准的质疑]  
ryao对氟化物在牙膏和水中的不同使用标准表示质疑，认为这两种使用方式不能共存。

• [氟化物与社会政策]  
fungiblecog指出，如果对含糖饮料征税或让牙科护理变得负担得起，水氟化可能就不必要了，但这种做法在美国往往被视为“共产主义”。

• [智商影响的实证质疑]  
lunarboy以讽刺的方式质疑那些认为氟化物降低智商的人，是否认为夏威夷的孩子智商高于其他州。

补充讨论：
• [过滤氟化物的问题]  
ourmandave提出了关于使用全屋过滤器去除氟化物的实际问题，指出其居住地水质差，但并未涉及氟化物具体问题。

• [历史书籍参考]  
piuantiderp提到了一本由Christopher Bryson撰写的书，暗示需要更多背景知识来理解水氟化争议。

• [最佳证据的请求]  
dataflow请求提供支持水氟化的最佳证据，显示了对讨论中事实基础的需求。

争议焦点：
• 氟化物对健康（特别是智商）的影响以及其必要性。
• 水氟化是否属于过度用药，以及氟化物的替代方案是否足够有效。
• 地方自治与居民自由选择权在水氟化问题上的适用性。
• 政治因素在反对水氟化中的作用。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Android应用权限、隐私问题以及原生应用与网页应用的对比

不同观点：
• **captn3m0**：提到了Android中的一个权限绕过漏洞（ACTION_MAIN），该问题未被Google修复，并建议将其提交到Android漏洞奖励计划（VDP）。同时引用了Stack Overflow上的相关问题。
• **turblety**：质疑原生应用的存在必要性，认为大多数应用可以被网页应用替代，且原生应用往往用于获取用户隐私信息。对应用商店的商业模式持批评态度。
• **DevKoala**：指出某些应用（如Swiggy）不需要了解用户是否安装了其他应用（如Xbox或Playstation），这种行为通常用于设备指纹识别。
• **zx8080**：质疑浏览器等应用为何需要列举已安装应用，认为没有必要。
• **andsoitis**：提到Android手机存在隐私缺陷，而iPhone没有此问题。
• **cheschire**：提问Windows应用是否能枚举所有打开窗口的标题，并探讨这种功能在现实中的可行性和潜在风险。
• **Tmpod**：提出可以通过LSPosed模块（如XPrivacyLua）来阻止或伪造应用权限，同时提到AppOps作为另一种选择。
• **bustling-noose**：指出大公司（如Swiggy和Zepto）会大量挖掘用户数据，部分用于自身利益，部分可能用于出售。同时提到外包开发带来的权限滥用问题。
• **hnburnsy**：批评Google对QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES权限的滥用，指出许多常见应用（如银行和相机应用）也拥有该权限。
• **einszwei**：对Google未修复权限绕过漏洞表示惊讶，认为Google留下了后门。
• **solardev**：从文化和语言角度看待印度用户的应用使用情况，表示对不同应用和表达方式感到新奇。
• **rkagerer**：询问是否可以在Play商店中查看应用允许与其通信的其他应用，以及是否可以在手机上查看和修改这些设置。
• **zer0zzz**：表示通过只使用手机自带应用和少数必需应用来避免权限滥用问题。
• **nickvec**：好奇为何该问题特别针对印度应用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了Android和iOS在隐私保护方面的对比，部分评论认为iOS在这方面表现更好。
• 对Google权限系统的批评较为集中，尤其是对QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES权限的滥用问题。
• 提到了用户数据挖掘和商业模式的讨论，特别是大公司如何利用和出售用户数据。
• 部分评论探讨了技术解决方案，如使用LSPosed模块和AppOps来保护隐私。
• 原生应用与网页应用的对比也是一个讨论热点，涉及应用商店的商业模式和隐私问题。

data.author: raphlinus
data.article_summary: Raph Levien在文章中回顾了七年前提出的通过Rust编写高效SIMD程序的愿景，指出目前Rust中编写SIMD代码的体验仍不理想，但已有进展和有希望的尝试。随着Linebender项目转向CPU/GPU混合渲染技术，SIMD对CPU性能至关重要，特别是在颜色转换和2D几何计算方面。文章通过计算sigmoid函数的例子展示了手写SIMD内联函数的复杂性，并强调了不同CPU架构下多版本和运行时调度的问题。虽然Rust语言层面尚未解决这些问题，但C++的Highway库提供了良好的多版本SIMD支持，值得借鉴。文章还讨论了几种可能的解决方案，包括使用类似Highway的库、macro-based方法（如multiversion和rust-target-feature-dispatch），以及基于零大小类型的多态函数方法（如pulp库）。Levien希望Rust能实现“无畏的SIMD”编程。

不同观点：
