Older Ivanpah Solar Plant in California Will Close Units, as Tech Shifts
By
James Leggate
Each of Ivanpah Solar Power Plant's three towers is surrounded by thousands of mirrors.
Photo by Dennis Schroeder/National Renewable Energy Laboratory
February 13, 2025
Power plant operator and co-owner NRG Energy Inc. is preparing to close down part of its
Ivanpah Solar Power Plant
in San Bernardino County, Calif., a little more than 11 years after it began operating. NRG agreed to terminate a pair of long-term purchase power agreements with utility Pacific Gas and Electric Co. for energy generated at the facility, which still uses technology the operator says has been surpassed by solar silicon photovoltaic generation.
Ivanpah is a concentrating solar power plant, which uses 173,500 heliostats—essentially mirrors on movable mounts so they can track the sun—to reflect sunlight onto boilers at the top of 450-ft-tall towers to make steam that turns turbines to generate power.
The plant has three units, each with its own tower surrounded by an array of heliostats, for a total capacity of 386 MW.
The utility contracted to purchase power from two of the units through 2039. But it said in a statement that in 2021— after the California Public Utilities Commission ordered investor-owned utilities to evaluate their energy sources—it identified its Ivanpah power purchase agreements as a potential area to find cost savings, with plant owners offering the opportunity to terminate the agreements. The companies, along with the U.S. Dept. of Energy, finalized negotiations to end the agreements last month. DOE
provided $1.6 billion in loan guarantees
for the project.
Houston-based NRG said in a statement that the negotiations allowed the department “to maximize the recovery of its loans and provide savings for California ratepayers.” An NRG representative did not say how much of the loan was repaid when asked, but said in a statement that the “concentrating solar power project was an innovative public-private partnership uniting government entities with private business in the advancement of renewable energy.”
A second utility, Southern California Edison, also contracted to buy power from the third Ivanpah unit through 2039. Its representative told ENR that the utility is in ongoing discussions with plant owners and DOE related to buyout of its Ivanpah contract.
NRG said it is now seeking approvals from state and federal officials to begin closing down the units next year for decommissioning. An NRG representative did not provide added details to ENR about the work or cost of decommissioning.
Concentrating Solar
Ivanpah was the largest concentrating solar power plant in the world at the time of its construction, and NRG said the project still demonstrated the technology’s viability.
Construction of the $2.2-billion plant started in 2010 with Bechtel Corp. as engineering, procurement and construction contractor. It began operations in late 2013 and remains the largest plant of its kind built in the U.S. .
At the time of Ivanpah’s construction, utility PG&E was investing in various kinds of developing clean energy technologies, including solar photovoltaic, hydroelectricity, wind, biomass and geothermal.
“It’s so important to support investment in different projects as we look to solve climate challenges,” said Don Howerton, PG&E senior director of commercial procurement, in a statement. “It’s not clear in the early stages what technologies will work best and be most affordable for customers.”
Improvements in solar photovoltaic wafers and panels and battery energy storage have made them more affordable options at large scale, Howerton added. The technologies have “raced ahead” in terms of affordability, according to PG&E.
Photovoltaic, or PV, technology uses silicon
crystals that are laminated into layers, often called wafers, with opposite charges.
When solar light hits the crystals, it creates a direct electric current through a process called the photovoltaic effect.
Ivanpah's generation is believed to have prevented 500,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually, according to the Energy Dept. But once operational, it drew criticism following reports that insects and birds were burned to death when they flew too close to the white-hot tower tops. A 2015 report prepared for the state by ecological consulting firm H.T. Harvey & Associates estimated the plant killed about 3,500 birds in its first year of operation.
Ivanpah also faced performance issues. In 2014, plant owners got
permission from state officials
to increase its annual limit of natural gas for its boilers from 328 million cu ft to 525 million cu ft, citing a need to use more fuel to power turbines to compensate for intermittent cloud cover.

data.title: Show HN: Cloud-Ready Postgres MCP Server
data.author: spennant
data.article_summary: PG-MCP是一个用于PostgreSQL数据库的模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器，专为AI代理设计，提供增强的数据库交互功能。主要特性包括：完整服务器实现、支持多数据库连接、丰富的目录信息、扩展上下文、查询解释和稳健的连接管理。它提供连接管理工具（如注册和断开数据库连接）、查询工具（执行SQL和分析查询计划），以及模式发现和数据访问资源。PG-MCP支持PostgreSQL扩展如PostGIS和pgvector，并通过YAML配置文件添加其他扩展。安装可通过Docker或手动进行，使用示例包括自然语言到SQL的转换。服务器默认以只读模式运行，确保安全。贡献者可扩展功能如添加更多扩展和优化查询建议。

PostgreSQL Model Context Protocol (PG-MCP) Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for PostgreSQL databases with enhanced capabilities for AI agents.
Overview
PG-MCP is a server implementation of the
Model Context Protocol
for PostgreSQL databases. It provides a comprehensive API for AI agents to discover, connect to, query, and understand PostgreSQL databases through MCP's resource-oriented architecture.
This implementation builds upon and extends the
reference Postgres MCP implementation
with several key enhancements:
Full Server Implementation
: Built as a complete server with SSE transport for production use
Multi-database Support
: Connect to multiple PostgreSQL databases simultaneously
Rich Catalog Information
: Extracts and exposes table/column descriptions from the database catalog
Extension Context
: Provides detailed YAML-based knowledge about PostgreSQL extensions like PostGIS and pgvector
Query Explanation
: Includes a dedicated tool for analyzing query execution plans
Robust Connection Management
: Proper lifecycle for database connections with secure connection ID handling
Features
Connection Management
Connect Tool
: Register PostgreSQL connection strings and get a secure connection ID
Disconnect Tool
: Explicitly close database connections when done
Connection Pooling
: Efficient connection management with pooling
Query Tools
pg_query
: Execute read-only SQL queries using a connection ID
pg_explain
: Analyze query execution plans in JSON format
Schema Discovery Resources
List schemas with descriptions
List tables with descriptions and row counts
Get column details with data types and descriptions
View table constraints and indexes
Explore database extensions
Data Access Resources
Sample table data (with pagination)
Get approximate row counts
Extension Context
Built-in contextual information for PostgreSQL extensions like:
PostGIS
: Spatial data types, functions, and examples
pgvector
: Vector similarity search functions and best practices
Additional extensions can be easily added via YAML config files.
Installation
Prerequisites
Python 3.13+
PostgreSQL database(s)
Using Docker
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/stuzero/pg-mcp.git
cd
pg-mcp
#
Build and run with Docker Compose
docker-compose up -d
Manual Installation
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/stuzero/pg-mcp.git
cd
pg-mcp
#
Create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
source
.venv/bin/activate
#
On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
#
Install using uv
uv sync --frozen
#
Run the server
python -m server.app
Usage
Testing the Server
The repository includes test scripts to verify server functionality:
#
Basic server functionality test
python test.py
"
postgresql://username:password@hostname:port/database
"
#
Claude-powered natural language to SQL conversion
python client/claude_cli.py
"
Show me the top 5 customers by total sales
"
The
claude_cli.py
script requires environment variables:
# .env file
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://username:password@hostname:port/database
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-anthropic-api-key
PG_MCP_URL=http://localhost:8000/sse
For AI Agents
Example prompt for use with agents:
Use the PostgreSQL MCP server to analyze the database.
Available tools:
- connect: Register a database connection string and get a connection ID
- disconnect: Close a database connection
- pg_query: Execute SQL queries using a connection ID
- pg_explain: Get query execution plans
You can explore schema resources via:
pgmcp://{conn_id}/schemas
pgmcp://{conn_id}/schemas/{schema}/tables
pgmcp://{conn_id}/schemas/{schema}/tables/{table}/columns
Architecture
This server is built on:
MCP
: The Model Context Protocol foundation
FastMCP
: Python library for MCP
asyncpg
: Asynchronous PostgreSQL client
YAML
: For extension context information
Security Considerations
The server runs in read-only mode by default (enforced via transaction settings)
Connection details are never exposed in resource URLs, only opaque connection IDs
Database credentials only need to be sent once during the initial connection
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Areas for expansion:
Additional PostgreSQL extension context files
More schema introspection resources
Query optimization suggestions
About
No description, website, or topics provided.

data.title: Bringing Record and Replay debugging everywhere on Linux
data.author: sidkshatriya
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者对`rr`调试工具的修改，使其能够在不访问CPU硬件性能计数器的情况下运行，从而可以在云虚拟机和容器等环境中使用。这解决了原版`rr`需要访问CPU硬件性能计数器才能工作的问题，扩展了其应用场景。作者将此变体称为"软件计数器模式" `rr`，并提供了构建、安装和运行的指南。

文章还解释了程序录制和回放的基本概念及其在调试中的重要性。通过录制程序运行时的所有输入和外部影响（如用户输入、网络调用、文件操作等），可以在回放时精确重现程序的运行状态，从而有效解决难以复现的程序错误问题。这种方法类似于视频回放，确保每次回放都与最初录制时一致，帮助开发者更准确地定位和修复错误。

Bringing Record and Replay everywhere
TL; DR
I've modified the awesome
rr
debugger
so that it can run
without needing access to CPU Hardware Performance counters.
This allows
rr
to be used in many more environments like cloud
VMs and containers where access to CPU HW performance counters is
usually disabled. Upstream
rr
requires access to CPU HW performance
counters to function, so this is a new feature and opens many
additional possibilities to debug your software with
rr
.
I call this variant,
Software Counters mode
rr
. Record and
Replay systems like
rr
deserve to be able to run everywhere and this
is my attempt at making this possible !
To build, install and run
Software Counters mode
rr please visit
https://github.com/sidkshatriya/rr.soft
Continue reading to understand some of the
basic concepts
behind Record and Replay and why it is such a powerful technique
when debugging programs.
What is program record and replay ? Why is it useful ?
When you watch a YouTube video, there is the unspoken expectation
that when you rewind or go forward an arbitrary number of seconds the
video is exactly the same as it had been when it was recorded !
You don't see something new in the video that was never there ! The
video and audio is exactly the same. In fact, if the video was
slightly different when you replayed it again and again
it would be extremely strange. You would probably think you were
going mad if the video were slightly different on each replay :-)
!
Allowing you to go forwards and backwards in time when viewing a
video is critical. Once a video is uploaded to the YouTube website,
it is essentially "frozen". This allows anybody to view the same
video any number of times and concentrate or learn from parts of
the video that are most interesting.
From replaying videos to programs
Let us shift focus from YouTube videos to computer programs.
Let's say you're attempting to run a program again and again because
you are facing some errors. When you try to debug an error, a good
strategy is try to give the program the same input because you want
to understand why it is failing for your specific input.
But sadly, every single time you run a program things are slightly
different:
Your user input like keystrokes may be the same but the timing of these
keystrokes can be subtly different. This could result in slightly different
internal state of a TUI (Text User Interface) program from run to run even though
the raw text you may have entered is the same
If the program has a graphical IDE, even though you may click on the same buttons, the
mouse speed or mouse path is slightly different from the last run or exact mouse click
locations differ by a few pixels
If the program makes network calls, remote servers might respond to requests
slightly differently from run to run -- there might be network failures, or
because the state of the remote servers is different they might still respond differently
If the program depends on time or random numbers the program might run a bit differently
as the time has changed or different random numbers are generated on every run
If the program depends on files on disk, the files may have gotten modified the last time the program
ran and as a result the error may not appear again. It may be difficult to restore the
files to the state in which the same error in the program happens again.
If the program is multithreaded, the different threads might interleave in slightly
differently ways from run to run so the results might be different
I hope you get the picture: every run of a sufficiently complex program is a special "Snowflake"
even though you may try to give it the same input.
So when a program goes wrong you have not one but two simultaneous
problems:
Find where the program bug is in the code
Try to set the conditions of your system and replicate
user input (and often subtle things like thread interleavings) in such a way that the program
when run again shows the same bug.
But as discussed above, so many things can change from run to run
! In fact, this is the age old problem of engineers "But it works
for me!" or alternatively "There was horrible error, likely to
appear in production... but I don't know how to get the error again
!"
Record and Replay to the rescue
What if while running the program you were simultaneously recording
it using a record/replay facility ? Think of a video camera of
sorts, but for programs. So that when you replay it back, it runs
in exactly the same way: the CPU instructions executed are exactly
the same, when files are "read" or "written" or when network calls
are made, the results are exactl

data.title: C. Elegans: The worm that no computer scientist can crack
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者在圣塔安娜风肆虐时运行了一种模拟蠕虫的程序，该程序旨在模拟显微镜下的线虫（*Caenorhabditis elegans*），作为OpenWorm开源项目的一部分。该项目自2011年以来一直尝试构建这种微小生物的数字 twin，以深入了解其神经系统与行为的关联。尽管项目尚未完全成功，模拟运行十小时仅能生成五秒的蠕虫蠕动视频，但其目标是创造出首个虚拟动物，揭示大脑与行为的关系。文章探讨了为何科学家要花费十多年时间研究这种蠕虫，引用物理学家费曼的名言：“我不能创造的，我便不理解。”文章强调，理解生命不仅需要分解其组成部分，还需要重建整个系统。尽管*C. elegans*体型微小，其对生物学的贡献却十分巨大，与多个诺贝尔奖研究相关。

The Santa Ana
winds were already blowing hard when I ran the first worm simulation. I’m no hacker, but it was easy enough: Open a Terminal shell, paste some commands from GitHub, watch characters cascade down the screen. Just like in the movies. I was scanning the passing code for recognizable words—
neuron
,
synapse
—when a friend came to pick me up for dinner. “One sec,” I yelled from my office. “I’m just running a worm on my computer.”
At the Korean restaurant, the energy was manic; the wind was bending palm trees at the waist and sending shopping carts skating across the parking lot. The atmosphere felt heightened and unreal, like a podcast at double speed.
You’re doing, what, a cybercrime?
my friend asked. Over the din, I tried to explain:
No, not a worm like Stuxnet. A worm like Richard Scarry.
By the time I got home it was dark, and the first sparks had already landed in
Altadena
. On my laptop, waiting for me in a volumetric pixel box, was the worm. Pointed at each end, it floated in a mist of particles, eerily stick-straight and motionless. It was, of course, not alive. Still, it looked deader than dead to me. “Bravo,” said Stephen Larson, when I reached him later that night. “You have achieved the ‘hello world’ state of the simulation.”
How to Get Computers—Before Computers Get You
Post-quantum algorithms, thermodynamic hardware, open source architectures, apocalypse-proof programming, and more: WIRED journeys to the freaky
frontiers of modern computing
.
Larson is a cofounder of
OpenWorm
, an open source software effort that has been trying, since 2011, to build a computer simulation of a microscopic nematode called
Caenorhabditis elegans
. His goal is nothing less than a digital twin of the real worm, accurate down to the molecule. If OpenWorm can manage this, it would be the first virtual animal—and an embodiment of all our knowledge not only about
C. elegans
, which is one of the most-studied animals in science, but about how brains interact with the world to produce behavior: the “holy grail,” as OpenWorm puts it, of systems biology.
Unfortunately, they haven’t managed it. The simulation on my laptop takes data culled from experiments done with living worms and translates it into a computational framework called c302, which then drives the simulated musculature of a
C. elegans
worm in a fluid dynamic environment—all in all, a simulation of how a worm squiggles forward in a flat plate of goo. It takes about 10 hours of compute time to generate five seconds of this behavior.
So much can happen in 10 hours. An ember can travel on the wind, down from the foothills and into the sleeping city. That night, on Larson’s advice, I tweaked the time parameters of the simulation, pushing beyond “hello world” and deeper into the worm’s uncanny valley. The next morning, I woke to an eerie orange haze, and when I pulled open my laptop, bleary-eyed, two things made my heart skip: Los Angeles was on fire. And my worm had moved.
At this point,
you may be asking yourself a very reasonable question. Back at the Korean place, between bites of banchan, my friend had asked it too. The question is this:
Uhh … why?
Why, in the face of everything our precarious green world endures, of all the problems out there to solve, would anyone spend 13 years trying to code a microscopic worm into existence?
By way of an answer, I’ll offer one of the physicist Richard Feynman’s most famous dictums:
What I cannot create, I do not understand.
For much of its history, biology has been a reductionist science, driven by the principle that the best way to understand the mind-boggling complexity of living things is to dissect them into their constituent parts—organs, cells, proteins, molecules. But life isn’t a clockwork; it’s a dynamic system, and unexpected things emerge from the interactions between all those little parts. To truly understand life, you can’t just break it down. You have to be able to put it back together, too.
The
C. elegans
nematode is a tiny worm, barely as long as a hair is wide, with less than a thousand cells in its body. Of those, only 302 are neurons—about as small as a brain can get. “I remember, when my first child was born, how proud I was when they reached the age they could count to 302,” said Netta Cohen, a computational neuroscientist who runs a
worm lab
at the University of Leeds. But there’s no shame in smallness, Cohen emphasized:
C. elegans
does a lot with a little. Unlike its more unpleasant cousins, it’s not a parasite, outsourcing its survival needs to bigger organisms. Instead, it’s what biologists call a “free-living” animal. “It can reproduce, it can eat, it can forage, it can escape,” Cohen said. “It’s born and it develops, and it ages and it dies—all in a millimeter.”
Worm people like Cohen are quick to tell you that no fewer than four Nobel Prizes have been awarded for work on
C. elegans
, which was the first animal to have both its genome sequenced

• userbinator认为bogantech的评论更像是为Altium做广告，并指出大多数笔记本电脑由少数OEM厂商生产，电路设计基于Intel/AMD的参考原理图，且彼此之间非常相似。他通过维基百科的链接支持其观点，强调了OEM厂商在设计上的相似性。

data.title: Electric power generation from Earth's rotation through its own magnetic field
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文报道了通过地球自转及其磁场产生电能的实验验证。传统观点认为无法利用地球磁场在其自转轴上产生电力，但作者通过使用特定软磁材料（锰锌铁氧体）构成的圆柱壳，在控制热电效应等干扰因素后，成功生成了持续的直流电压和电流。实验显示，当圆柱壳的长轴与地球旋转速度和磁场垂直时，电压和电流达到峰值；当设备旋转至壳体与速度平行时，电压和电流为零；再旋转90度后，电压和电流反向达到峰值。此外，实心圆柱体和磁雷诺数高的壳体均未产生电压。该实验验证了理论预测，未来可探索提高电压和电流的方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用地球旋转能量发电的可行性及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [ziofill] 和 [ninetyninenine]、[ChrisNorstrom] 认为，如果大量使用这种发电方式，可能会减缓地球的自转速度。ziofill 通过公式计算出地球的旋转动能约为 5e36 焦耳，并指出虽然总量很大，但大规模使用可能影响地球自转。ChrisNorstrom 也提出了类似的问题，担心大规模使用会减缓地球自转。

• [vessenes] 则关注发电设备的材料科学问题，提出是否可以通过找到合适的材料将发电设备缩小到原来的 1/1000，并讨论了这种缩小是否可以无限进行。他对这种技术的实际应用表现出较大兴趣，尤其是将设备缩小后在并行阵列中的应用潜力。

• [threeseed] 提供了具体的电流和电压数据，计算出30厘米壳体的总功率为0.44皮瓦，给出了实际操作中的具体功率数值，但没有讨论宏观影响。

• [qnleigh] 提供了一个关于该主题的快速阅读链接，指向《Nature》杂志的一篇文章，帮助读者进一步了解相关内容。

• [Kerbonut] 提出了一个相关但不同的想法，即利用太阳风和地球磁场作为能量转换的工具，从太阳获取动能转化为电能，而不是直接影响地球的自转。

• [bastawhiz] 对摘要中的链接表示困惑，质疑其用途或相关性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于利用地球旋转能量是否会导致地球自转减缓，特别是在大规模应用的情况下。
• 讨论还涉及技术实现的可能性，尤其是材料科学的进展能否使设备缩小，同时保持发电效率。
• 一些评论提供了具体的技术数据和外部资源链接，帮助深入理解该技术的实际应用和科学背景。

Title:
Experimental demonstration of electric power generation from Earth's rotation through its own magnetic field
Authors:
Christopher F. Chyba
,
Kevin P. Hand
,
Thomas H. Chyba
View a PDF of the paper titled Experimental demonstration of electric power generation from Earth's rotation through its own magnetic field, by Christopher F. Chyba and 2 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Earth rotates through the axisymmetric part of its own magnetic field, but a simple proof shows that it is impossible to use this to generate electricity in a conductor rotating with
this http URL
, we previously identified implicit assumptions underlying this proof and showed theoretically that these could be violated and the proof circumvented. This requires using a soft magnetic material with a topology satisfying a particular mathematical condition and a composition and scale favoring magnetic diffusion, i.e. having a low magnetic Reynolds number Rm (C.F. Chyba, K.P. Hand, Electric power generation from Earth's rotation through its own magnetic field. Phys. Rev. Applied 6, 014017-1-18 (2016)). Here we realize these requirements with a cylindrical shell of manganese-zinc ferrite. Controlling for thermoelectric and other potentially confounding effects (including 60 Hz and RF background), we show that this small demonstration system generates a continuous DC voltage and current of the (low) predicted magnitude. We test and verify other predictions of the theory: voltage and current peak when the cylindrical shell's long axis is orthogonal to both Earth's rotational velocity v and magnetic field; voltage and current go to zero when the entire apparatus (cylindrical shell together with current leads and multimeters) is rotated 90 degrees to orient the shell parallel to v; voltage and current again reach a maximum but of opposite sign when the apparatus is rotated a further 90 degrees; an otherwise-identical solid MnZn cylinder generates zero voltage at all orientations; and a highRm cylindrical shell produces zero voltage. We also reproduce the effect at a second experimental location. The purpose of these experiments was to test the existence of the predicted effect. Ways in which this effect might be scaled to generate higher voltage and current may now be investigated.

43520716.article_summary: 本文报道了通过地球自转及其磁场产生电能的实验验证。传统观点认为无法利用地球磁场在其自转轴上产生电力，但作者通过使用特定软磁材料（锰锌铁氧体）构成的圆柱壳，在控制热电效应等干扰因素后，成功生成了持续的直流电压和电流。实验显示，当圆柱壳的长轴与地球旋转速度和磁场垂直时，电压和电流达到峰值；当设备旋转至壳体与速度平行时，电压和电流为零；再旋转90度后，电压和电流反向达到峰值。此外，实心圆柱体和磁雷诺数高的壳体均未产生电压。该实验验证了理论预测，未来可探索提高电压和电流的方法。

data.title: Prepare()-ing for execution: a new API for process creation
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为`prepare()`的新API，旨在简化UNIX中使用fork+exec创建进程的过程。与传统的fork+exec方法相比，prepare()简化了控制流，避免了复杂的返回处理，同时保留了配置环境的灵活性。调用prepare()后，当前线程进入“准备状态”，创建一个初始进程，但不改变内存映射。然后可以配置环境，并调用`prep_execve()`执行新程序或使用`prep_exit()`终止子进程。该API解决了fork+exec使用复杂和spawn难以扩展的问题，提供了更直接的进程创建和配置方式。文中还提供了示例代码和API详细说明。

README.md
UNIX famously uses fork+exec to create processes, a simple API that is nevertheless quite tricky to use correctly and that comes with a bunch of problems. The alternative, spawn, as used by VMS, Windows NT and recently POSIX, fixes many of these issues but it overly complex and makes it hard to add new features.
prepare() is a proposed API to simplify process creation. When calling prepare(), the current thread enters “preparation state.” That means, a nascent process is created and the current thread is moved to the context of this process, but without changing memory maps (this is similar to how vfork() works). Inside the nascent process, you can configure the environment as desired and then call prep_execve() to execute a new program. On success, prep_execve() leaves preparation state, moving the current thread back to the parent's process context and returns (!) the pid of the now grownup child. You can also use prep_exit() to abort the child without executing a new process, it similarly returns the pid of the now zombified child.
Here's an example for executing a child with stdout redirected to /dev/null:
int stfu(char *prog, char *argv[]) {
if (prepare(NULL) == -1)
return (-1);
int fd = open("/dev/null", O_WRONLY);
if (fd == -1) {
return (prep_exit(1));
}
dup2(fd, 1);
close(fd);
int pid = prep_execve(prog, argv, environ);
if (pid == -1) {
return (prep_exit(1));
}
return (pid);
}
The key advantage of this API is that it has completely linear control flow like spawn, while preserving the flexible builder-pattern provided by fork+exec. No double-return shenanigans like with fork and execve. And because the nascent process shares memory with the parent, it's possible to communicate failure to execute and similar stuff using simple variables.

data.title: Making WebGL typesafe in Idris 2
data.author: srid
data.article_summary: 这篇文章记录了作者学习Idris语言和探索类型安全性的过程，特别是尝试将WebGL规范的所有文档融入类型中，以实现"构造正确的程序"。文章以日志形式呈现，记录了作者的思考和开发过程，包括以下主题：从基础三角形绘制到动画实现，初步性能测试，线性类型问题，从IO monad转向GL monad，代码质量改进，初次使用依赖类型，确保uniforms属于绑定程序，隐式参数和monad转换器，单调性与monadic错误，线性代数与线性类型的不佳结合，进展缓慢且挫折不断，重新振作，限制参数为列表，再次绑定程序，Hoare状态失败，以及暂时中断。文章强调了作者观点和意见的变化，并预示可能会有错误。

data.title: I Don't Allow AI Notetakers in My Coaching Sessions
data.author: adrianhoward
data.article_summary: 本文作者是一位教练，她解释了为何在自己的 coaching 课程中不使用AI笔记工具。她认为教练的核心价值在于为客户创造一个安全、支持的空间，帮助他们自主发现和探索想法，而不是单纯提取“正确”答案。虽然AI技术有其用途，但在教练对话中，过度的记录和跟踪会破坏这种信任和自由的氛围，影响深层次的转变。作者强调，教练过程的美妙之处在于人际交流和当下的存在感，而不是所有细节的记录。因此，她目前选择不让AI笔记工具介入 coaching 课程，以保持对话的纯粹性和深度。

43518042.article_content:
Why I Don’t Allow AI Notetakers in My Coaching Sessions
One of the core values of
coaching
, at least in my practice, is creating and holding space for the coachee. A space where they can think the unthinkable, explore new perspectives, and assess their thoughts in a way that leads to clarity, direction, and—hopefully—progress.
I know many of my coachees choose to work with me not just for my experience, but because of the energy I bring into our conversations. This energy is positive, improvement-driven, and focused on moving forward.
Coaching, in this sense, isn’t about extracting the “right” answers from people. It’s about helping them unlock their own insights, in a space where they feel supported rather than scrutinized. The image below helps illustrate this concept—you can see that “telling” actions, like solving people’s problems for them or giving advice leads to little to no development, while “asking” actions like providing feedback or challenging their thinking leads to long-term development.
A coach’s actions exist on a spectrum from telling to asking. The more the action falls into the “telling” category, the less it leads to long-term development.
That’s why, in most of my coaching sessions, even the most engaged and proactive coachees rarely take extensive notes. At most, they jot down three or four sentences—usually by hand. The ones who begin with detailed notetaking tend to drop it after our second or third session, once they realize I’m not here to quiz them on their progress. I trust them to take notes when they need to, in a way that serves them best.
I like when people experiment with new technologies. I’m a big AI user myself. But I also have a deep sense of unease when I see the increasing drive to track everything, record everything, optimize everything. I feel this irritation with health and fitness trackers that turn movement into metrics, with augmented reality glasses that layer screens over real-life moments, and, yes, with AI notetakers in coaching conversations.
I get using these tools for business meetings where decisions and action items need to be captured. But let’s be real—there’s a lot of beauty in human-to-human conversations. In the pauses. In the way someone takes a moment to find their words. In the trust that builds when people know they are speaking freely, without an invisible third party documenting every thought.
The feeling of
something
listening in on a deeply personal coaching conversation creates a subtle, but significant, shift. And that’s enough for me to say no.
For now, I’ve decided not to allow AI notetakers in my coaching sessions. Not because I reject the technology, but because I believe the essence of coaching—real transformation—happens in the moments that don’t need to be recorded.
Maybe that will change. Maybe I’ll see a use case that convinces me otherwise. But right now, I stand by this: Coaching is about trust, presence, and exploration. If recording everything gets in the way of that, I’d rather leave the AI at the door.
Consider this article a gentle reminder that you don't need to universally adopt a new technology just because it's there. It's worth spending some time reflecting on whether the technology is genuinely serving you or if it might be leading to some less-than-optimal unintended consequences.

data.title: RFK, Jr. Laying Off Entire Office of Infectious Disease and HIV/Aids Policy
data.author: pmags
data.article_summary: 美国卫生与公众服务部（HHS）部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪（RFK, Jr.）计划大幅裁减HHS员工，其中包括解散整个传染病与艾滋病政策办公室（OIDP）。此举是HHS精简和重组的一部分，总员工数将从约82,000人减至62,000人，涉及食品和药物管理局、疾病控制与预防中心等多个机构的岗位削减。OIDP负责多项国家战略的实施，如国家艾滋病战略和疫苗计划，其解散将导致大量经验和专业知识的流失。此外，多个外部科学专家咨询委员会也可能被解散，包括血液和组织安全咨询委员会及总统艾滋病咨询委员会等。然而，肯尼迪尚未提供明确的计划说明如何重新配置这些职能，导致卫生和公共卫生界对未来安排感到困惑和担忧。

  - 引用科学研究和专家意见，强调疫苗的安全性和有效性，驳斥关于疫苗副作用的未经证实的指控。

meeting held by US President Donald Trump on March 24, 2025, is reportedly laying off the entire staff of the U.S. government’s Office of Infectious Disease and HIV/AIDS Policy. (Photo by BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP via Getty Images)
AFP via Getty Images
The U.S. is still reeling from the COVID-19 pandemic with more and more long COVID cases emerging. Bird flu is
a growing threat
. Measles outbreaks have been occurring. Antibiotic-resistant organisms continue to spread in healthcare settings. So what do you do next if you are in charge of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, which is supposed to protect the health of humans in the U.S.? How about lay off the entire staff of the U.S. government’s Office of Infectious Disease and HIV/AIDS Policy?
Office of Infectious Disease ‘Gutting’ Is Part Of RFK, Jr.’s Downsizing And Restructuring Of HHS
Yep, that’s the word from various federal health officials and external experts who work with the OIDP.
Alexander Tin reporting for
CBS News
described it as gutting the OIDP. It’s apparently part of the whole HHS downsizing and restructuring plan with Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., as the Secretary of HHS that’s been
posted as a fact sheet
. That fact sheet indicates that the number of HHS employees will be slashed from around 82,000 to 62,000. This will include cutting around 3,500 jobs at the Food and Drug Administration, 2,400 at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and 1,200 at the National Institutes of Health.
The problem is that the general public may not be fully aware of all that OIDP does and the expertise that will be lost. Chances are that more people are more familiar with the acronym GOT, which stands for Game of Thrones, than the acronym OIDP. But the cuts at HHS are beginning to resemble the plots of GOT in different ways. Each week, it’s not clear who will be gone next.
OIDP Serves Important Roles In Infectious Disease Prevention And Control
The
stated mission of the OIDP
is “to provide strategic leadership and management, while encouraging collaboration, coordination, and innovation among federal agencies and stakeholders to reduce the burden of infectious diseases.” This includes implementing various national plans to prevent and control infectious diseases. For example, there’s the National HIV/AIDS Strategy, Vaccines National Strategic Plan, Viral Hepatitis National Strategic Plan and the Sexually Transmitted Infections National Strategic Plan. The OIDP also directs different initiatives such as initiatives to end the HIV epidemic in the U.S., prevent healthcare-associated infections and control tick-borne diseases.
Also potentially going poof are the various advisory committees of external scientific experts that the OIPD has been maintaining. This includes the Advisory Committee on Blood and Tissue Safety and Availability, Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS (PACHA), Presidential Advisory Council on Combating Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria (PACCARB) and National Vaccine Advisory Committee (NVAC). In fact, sources have told me that the PACCARB has already been disbanded.

RFK, Jr. Has Not Yet Provided A Clear Plan On Who Now Will Handle Different Aspects Of Infectious Disease Control
Tearing stuff down is a typically whole lot easier than building up things. For example, asking, “Who can trash a house” will probably get more takers such as many of your classmates if you are in high school than asking, “Who can build a house?” By jettisoning the staff and advisors for the OIDP, the federal government will lose years and years of experience and expertise.
Of course, there is the possibility that some of these initiatives, plans and advisory committees will somehow resurface in some other forms in the near future. However, neither RFK, Jr. nor the rest of the Trump Administration have provided a clear and adequately detailed plan to date of how HSS specifically will be reconfigured and what scientific, health and public health efforts will be covered by what part of this new version of HHS and in what way. For example, no one whom I have talked to at HHS and in the infectious disease community knows where in HHS the prevention and control of healthcare associated infections will eventually reside and how many people will be involved in such efforts. data.article_summary: 联邦卫生机构的裁员计划预计将导致卫生与公众服务部（HHS）裁减20,000个职位，其中包括传染病与艾滋病政策办公室（OIDP）的全体员工。该办公室负责多项关键健康项目，如提高儿童疫苗接种率的“让我们面对现实”活动，以及终结美国艾滋病流行的计划。OIDP还管理国家疫苗计划，协调疫苗开发和安全性。此外，少数族裔健康办公室也可能被解散。这些裁员是HHS restructuring的一部分，旨在成立一个新的"健康美国机构"（AHA），吸收包括药物滥用和心理健康服务管理局等其他部门。目前，具体实施细节和长期领导人人选尚不明确。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：年轻人为何会支持被认为是保守的政党

不同观点：
• 一方认为年轻人投票给保守政党（被评论者称为“反性、支持警察”的政党）是令人惊讶的，因为该党派并不支持像迷幻药物合法化这样的进步或自由立场。这暗示了投票者可能没有关注自身的长期利益或享乐需求。评论者对年轻选民的选择感到失望，认为他们的选择与其应有的开放态度不符。

• 另一方可能暗示，年轻人投票给这个政党可能不是因为其社会或文化立场（如对性或药物的态度），而是因为该政党在其他议题上的吸引力，例如经济政策、国家安全或执法力度。支持警察的立场可能被视为对社会秩序和安全的重视，而不是简单的保守主义。

补充讨论：
• 评论中隐含的争议焦点在于年轻人对政党的期待和他们实际投票行为之间的差距。评论者认为年轻人应该支持更自由、开放的立场，而非保守或“反性”的立场。

• 评论还提到了迷幻药物合法化的问题，暗示在某些选民群体中，尤其是年轻人中，可能期望更开放的药物政策。这表明在文化和生活方式上的开放性与保守政党政策之间的矛盾。

• 该评论还引发了关于选民动机的讨论：选民是否根据文化议题（如性、药物政策）投票，还是更关注实际政策（如经济、安全）等更广泛的问题。这揭示了选民行为中的复杂性，尤其是在年轻选民中的多样化立场。

43521261.article_content:
Impact of cuts at federal health agencies
How cuts at federal health agencies could impact Americans' health care
02:30
The entire staff of the federal government's Office of Infectious Disease and HIV/AIDS Policy is expected to be laid off, multiple federal health officials told CBS News Friday. The moves are part of a broader
restructuring plan
ordered by Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that involves cutting 20,000 HHS positions.
Much of the government's efforts to buoy lagging
childhood vaccination rates
nationwide have been run through OIDP, including a new campaign called "Let's Get Real" that had launched in the final months of the Biden administration to provide resources and information to health care providers talking to hesitant parents.
"Spreading the truth saves lives, so use our resources to help parents understand how vaccines work, why they're safe, and how they help protect kids," the department had said of the
campaign
after it was launched.
The Office of Minority Health has also been informed that it should expect to be dissolved, sources said.
However, multiple officials said that written notices of layoffs had not yet been received by HHS employees.
Senior federal health officials initially said Friday they were expecting that official notices of the cuts would be issued in the afternoon, but acknowledged that the timing of the letters could slide into the weekend, similar to the cuts to HHS
probationary workers
sought by the Trump administration earlier this year.
OIDP, overseen by the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health or OASH, had numbered around 60 employees at the end of the Biden administration. The cuts come as the Trump administration is trying to merge the other offices in OASH into a new HHS agency called the Administration for a Health America, or AHA.
HHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the potential layoffs.
The
National Vaccine Program
has also been run by OIDP, which works with an advisory committee to coordinate the department's agencies to develop vaccines, oversee their safety and increase their availability and use.
Other
initiatives
overseen by OIDP include the Ending the HIV Epidemic in the U.S. program, which was launched by President Trump during his first term. It is unclear what will happen to those initiatives, which Congress had approved funding for.
OIDP had previously been among several overseen by former Assistant Secretary for Health
Rachel Levine
under the Biden administration.
It is unclear whether other HHS agencies that had been overseen by Levine, like the office tasked with updating the federal
dietary guidelines
, will also be cut. That office had been the target of criticism under Kennedy's Make America Health Again agenda.
The new AHA agency would also absorb the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration and Health Resources and Services Administration, according to a
fact sheet
published by the department.
Who would lead the AHA in the long term is unclear. For now, officials have been told to expect HRSA's administrator
Thomas Engels
to head AHA.
Kennedy's aides have told senior health officials that they are targeting a quick turnaround to launch the AHA, with some implementation goals to be hit within the next 10 days.

补充讨论：
• 评论中隐含的争议焦点在于年轻人对政党的期待和他们实际投票行为之间的差距。评论者认为年轻人应该支持更自由、开放的立场，而非保守或“反性”的立场。

• 评论还提到了迷幻药物合法化的问题，暗示在某些选民群体中，尤其是年轻人中，可能期望更开放的药物政策。这表明在文化和生活方式上的开放性与保守政党政策之间的矛盾。

• 该评论还引发了关于选民动机的讨论：选民是否根据文化议题（如性、药物政策）投票，还是更关注实际政策（如经济、安全）等更广泛的问题。这揭示了选民行为中的复杂性，尤其是在年轻选民中的多样化立场。

data.title: Remove improper ideology: Vance tasked with purging the Smithsonian Institution
data.author: zfg
data.article_summary: 2025年3月，美国总统特朗普签署行政命令，指示史密森学会及其附属机构，包括教育中心和国家动物园，清除“不当意识形态”，恢复“历史的真实与理智”。该命令由副总统JD Vance负责执行，旨在删除任何“贬低美国共同价值观、基于种族分裂美国、或宣扬与联邦法律和政策不符的意识形态”的项目或展览。具体关注种族、奴隶制和吉姆·克劳法的描绘，特别是美国非裔历史文化博物馆的展品。命令还要求恢复过去五年内被移除的邦联纪念碑，以抵制“反美意识形态”。这是史密森学会175年历史上最大的行政干预。

43520560.article_content:
"Remove improper ideology": Trump puts Vance in charge of purging the Smithsonian Institution
The White House wants the quasi-independent network of museums to remove "improper ideology" from its collections
By
Griffin Eckstein
Published March 28, 2025 12:40PM (EDT)
Smithsonian's National Museum of African American History and Culture
(Getty/Preston Keres)
--
Shares
Facebook
Twitter
Reddit
Email
President
Donald Trump
directed the
Smithsonian Institution
and Department of the Interior on Thursday to sanitize exhibitions, possibly restore Confederate monuments and remove objectionable pieces to restore “truth and sanity to American history," part of what he described as a war on “corrosive ideology.”
An
executive order
on Thursday instructs the Smithsonian museum system to axe any projects or exhibitions that “degrade shared American values, divide Americans based on race, or promote programs or ideologies inconsistent with Federal law and policy.”
Related
The long fight to build the National Museum of African American History and Culture
The order instructs Vice President
JD Vance
to "remove improper ideology” from the Smithsonian’s museums, education and research centers and the National Zoo, per the order. The order is the biggest executive reach into the quasi-independent trust in its more than 175 year history.
One specific issue raised by the order is the depiction of race, the legacy of slavery and Jim Crow laws, and other historical narratives in the Smithsonian’s collections.
The order calls for a purge of “divisive narratives that distort our shared history,” including works or exhibitions that reinforce the notion that “race is not a biological reality but a social construct.” At the heart of the attack are collections in the
National Museum of African American History and Culture,
one of the five
most popular
D.C. museums in 2024, and the American Women’s History Museum.
Another provision of the decree appears to take action to restore monuments to Confederate leaders on federal land under the auspices of rejecting “anti-American ideology.”
The head of the Department of the Interior is directed to restore monuments that have “have been improperly removed or changed in the last five years to perpetuate a false revision of history,” per a White House
fact sheet.

主要讨论点：波兰经济增长及其原因

不同观点：
• [rasz的观点] 认为波兰自1990年以来，经过35年，终于实现了当时总统候选人瓦文萨承诺的“在波兰建立第二个日本”的目标。这表明波兰经过多年发展，终于在经济上取得了显著进步。
  
• [0dayz的观点] 指出波兰的经济增长在很大程度上得益于欧盟的资金支持，波兰从欧盟获得的资金超过了其缴纳的费用，这是经济增长的一个重要因素。

• [xqcgrek2的观点] 强调在讨论GDP时应使用购买力平价（PPP）而非名义GDP，暗示用不同的经济指标可能会影响对波兰经济成就的评价。

补充讨论：
• rasz的观点带有历史背景，提到1990年瓦文萨的竞选承诺，并用时间跨度来证明这一承诺的实现，但未提及欧盟的作用。
• 0dayz的观点引入了欧盟资金对波兰经济的影响，指出了外部支持对波兰经济增长的贡献，这与rasz的纯粹内部发展视角形成对比。
• xqcgrek2则关注于经济数据的准确性，强调GDP的衡量方式可能影响对波兰经济成就的看法，这为讨论增加了技术层面的复杂性。

争议焦点：波兰经济成功的主要驱动因素，是源自内部努力还是外部支持，以及如何正确评估其经济成就（使用何种GDP指标）。

data.author: swatson741
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SML（Standard ML）作为编程语言在教育和实际应用中的价值

不同观点：
• [trollied] 认为SML作为大学计算机科学学位的第一门编程语言非常合适。它帮助学生在没有太多编程背景的情况下站在同一起跑线上，并且有助于教授递归等概念。该用户对使用SML的体验非常积极。

• [toolslive] 高度赞赏SML，认为它即使老旧但依然在很多方面优于后来的语言，例如类型推断、模式匹配和尾调用优化等特性。同时，SML的性能也非常优秀。该评论暗示SML应作为编程语言设计者的入门考试内容，显示出对SML的高度认可。

• [cantrevealname] 提供了一个澄清，指出SML不是机器学习（Machine Learning），而是一种名为Standard ML的编程语言，并提供了相关的维基百科链接以供参考。

• [swatson741] 认为SML值得学习，尤其是模式匹配功能，但指出其模式匹配功能不如Lisp全面。同时，SML的数据类型和类的表现力不如其他语言。该评论对SML持部分肯定态度，但也指出其局限性。

• [msarnoff] 分享了一个关于SML的小知识，指出SML的函数组合运算符使用小写字母"o"，这与数学符号一致，显示出SML在某些语法设计上的优雅。

• [uzername] 分享了个人经验，提到在本科编译器课程中使用了SML，并且因为这门课而开始探索其他编程语言。这显示出SML在激发学生对编程语言兴趣方面的积极作用。

补充讨论：
• SML的模式匹配功能是一个被多次提及的优点，但不同用户对其与Lisp等其他语言的对比有不同看法。
• SML的教学价值和其在学术环境中的应用被多位用户肯定，特别是在帮助初学者建立编程基础方面。
• 对SML的局限性也有所讨论，如模式匹配的限制和数据类型表现力的不足。

争议焦点：
• SML与Lisp在模式匹配和数据类型表现力上的对比是讨论中的一个争议点，[swatson741]认为Lisp在某些方面更优越。

data.title: Kalua: An OpenWrt extension for building large mesh-networks
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: Kalua是一个基于OpenWRT的硬件独立扩展工具，使用POSIX shell作为主要语言，用于设置、监控和管理大规模WiFi mesh网络。它支持多种功能，如计费、 captive portal（网页登录）、数据保留和QoS等。Kalua提供自动化脚本帮助用户构建自定义OpenWRT固件，适用于不同硬件和用例。用户可以通过克隆Git仓库并运行提供的脚本轻松构建和定制自己的网络环境。文档和支持可通过社区及咨询服务获取。

data.title: Just Write a Test for It
data.author: dmit
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在Rust项目中处理数据库迁移时遇到的一个问题：在已有数据的表中添加一个NOT NULL列但没有提供DEFAULT值，导致部署出错。尽管初始测试套件未能发现此问题，作者没有止步于简单修复，而是借助Rust生态中的`sqlparser`库，编写了一个集成测试来自动检测类似问题。作者赞赏Rust激励其追求更高质量的解决方案，并详细描述了如何利用`sqlparser`实现该检测功能。最终，作者成功预防了未来可能出现的类似错误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据库迁移测试的有效性及复杂性，特别是关于预填充数据库与空数据库的测试方法，以及使用SQL解析工具的合理性。

不同观点：
• **karparov**：认为现有的测试套件有漏洞，因为测试总是从一个空数据库开始，应用所有迁移后再运行测试代码。建议使用预填充数据库进行测试，以捕获更广泛的问题，而不仅仅是检查非空或默认值。

• **kobzol（博文作者）**：澄清博文的重点并不是解决数据库迁移的所有问题，而是展示在Rust中完成特定任务的简便性。他提到提供一个好的错误信息也是有价值的，即使有更通用的解决方案。

• **dreghgh**：反对博文中的方法，认为应该在运行迁移之前将数据放入数据库架构中，这样可以捕捉到各种未预见的错误，而不是仅仅解决特定类型的问题。

• **kleiba**：认为博文内容令人失望，主要讲述了在Rust中解析SQL查询的惊喜，没有太大的阅读价值。

• **switch007**：提到一个相关的工具——"squawk"，这是一个专注于迁移的PostgreSQL代码检查工具，可能可以解决此类问题。

• **lbreakjai**：分享了在之前工作中实现类似Neon分支的经验，每个MR都会克隆"public"架构到一个特定MR的架构中，然后运行迁移和集成测试，这样可以捕获一些在实际运行中才会出现的错误。

• **nikolayasdf123**：认为测试过于复杂，比要测试的DDL语句本身还要复杂，这种现象是人们不愿意写测试的原因之一，建议让测试变得更简单和易于维护。

• **hardwaresofton**：建议开发一个通用的SQL代码检查工具，类似于sqlint，但更专注于语义而非语法。

• **conradludgate**：推荐使用Neon的branching功能，可以在不影响生产数据和性能的情况下运行迁移测试，并提到未来可能会开发更多迁移工具。

• **bilalq**：支持使用Neon这样的支持分支的无服务器数据库进行迁移测试，可以轻松地在每个PR更改时运行，测试迁移是否对真实数据安全。

• **null_deref**：对文章中的Rust生态系统没有经过CR就直接链接PR的做法表示疑问，质疑这是否是大型语言标准库的标准做法。

• **bobnamob**：担心引入一个SQL解析器作为依赖会增加攻击面和漏洞风险，特别是在当前供应链攻击频发的情况下。

• **earnestinger**：指出文章没有说明SQL解析器是针对哪种数据库（如PostgreSQL或MySQL），建议提供更具体的信息。

• **bsaul**：作为非Rust开发者，对Rust代码中的复杂生命周期注释和长泛型类型感到困惑，询问这种代码在实践中是否常见。

补充讨论：
- 测试复杂性与实用性的平衡是争议的一个焦点，部分评论者认为复杂的测试不如简单易读的测试有用。
- 使用预填充数据库进行测试的建议得到了部分支持，尤其是结合Neon分支功能的具体实现方法。
- 引入SQL解析工具作为依赖的合理性及其潜在的安全风险也被提出并讨论。

43480459.article_content:
This is a short appreciation post about Rust continuously guiding me towards doing The Right Thing™.
Google Summer of Code 2025
is just around the corner, which means that a bunch of new contributors started sending pull requests to various Rust projects. One of the most popular projects seems to be
bors
, a from-scratch implementation of a merge queue bot that we aim to use to manage pull requests in the main
Rust compiler repository
.
In the past couple of weeks, I have reviewed and merged tens of PRs in bors. Sadly, soon after I figured out that some of them broke the (staging) deployment of the bot. This was quite annoying, because I was deliberately trying to design the bot, tests and CI so that something like this shouldn’t happen. In practice, we would probably detect this issue in the staging environment, so it hopefully wouldn’t reach production, but it’s still a situation that I would like to avoid as much as possible.
After investigating for a bit, I realized that the issue was in an SQL migration that looked something like this:
ALTER
TABLE
foo
ADD
COLUMN
bar
NOT
NULL
;
It looked innocent enough at a first glance, until I realized that adding a
NOT NULL
column to an already populated table without providing some
DEFAULT
value for the existing rows is not a good idea. This wasn’t caught by the existing test suite (even though it runs almost 200 end-to-end tests), because it always starts from an empty database, applies all migrations and only then runs the test code.
I fixed the bug, but I didn’t want to stop there. My programming experience
1
has taught me to (almost) always try to figure out how can I make sure that a specific bug (or ideally a whole class of bugs) won’t ever happen again after we first fix it. In this case, it seemed a bit tricky at first though, as the problem was in the structure of arbitrary SQL statements.
I started by adding a
warning
to the bors development guide, urging people not to write migrations like this. While this is better than nothing, it’s clear that in practice, documentation alone is a very weak protection against similar bugs.
If this was any other technology or language, I would most likely stop there and just call it a day. But with Rust, I somehow feel encouraged (and empowered!) to go the extra mile and try to make sure that I did everything I could to prevent future problems (and urgent pings when something breaks :) ).
But what could we do here? Surely we won’t
parse and examine SQL queries
just for a single test?
…Well, after thinking about it for a while, why couldn’t we? I knew that there is a crate for parsing SQL called
sqlparser
. I was worried that it would have hundreds of dependencies and would be overkill for writing a single test, but when I added it as a
dev
dependency, I found out that it only has around three tiny dependencies (that can even be disabled if needed) and compiles pretty quickly.
Standing on the shoulder of giants and armed with a production-grade SQL parser, I started writing an integration test that goes through the
migrations
directory, parses each SQL file and detects situations where a
NOT NULL
column is added without a
DEFAULT
clause.
sqlparser
supports the
Visitor
pattern, which made the implementation quite easy. My solution is probably not bulletproof and there are certainly some cases that it could miss, but it should be enough to find the problematic situation in typical migration queries.
The goal of this blog post isn’t to show how to use
sqlparser
, so I won’t dig into it, but if you’re interested, you can examine the full test code below (it’s just ~100 lines of code, excluding imports):
Test code

itertools
::
Itertools
;
use
sqlparser
::
ast
::{
AlterColumnOperation
,
AlterTableOperation
,
ColumnOption
,
Ident
,
ObjectName
,
Statement
,
Visit
,
Visitor
,
};
use
sqlparser
::
dialect
::
PostgreSqlDialect
;
use
sqlparser
::
parser
::
Parser
;
use
std
::
collections
::{
BTreeSet
,
HashSet
};
use
std
::
ffi
::
OsStr
;
use
std
::
ops
::
ControlFlow
;
use
std
::
path
::
PathBuf
;
struct
CheckNotNullWithoutDefault
{
error
:
Option
<
String
>
,
columns_set_to_not_null
:
HashSet
<
(
ObjectName
,
Ident
)
>
,
columns_set_default_value
:
HashSet
<
(
ObjectName
,
Ident
)
>
,
}
impl
Visitor
for
CheckNotNullWithoutDefault
{
type
Break
=
();
fn
pre_visit_statement
(
&
mut
self
,
statement
:
&
Statement
)
->
ControlFlow
<
Self
::

>
{
if
let
Statement
::
AlterTable
{
operations
,
name
,
..
}
=
statement
{
for
op
in
operations
{
match
op
{
AlterTableOperation
::
AddColumn
{
column_def
,
..
}
=>
{
let
has_not_null
=
column_def
.options
.iter
()
.any
(|
option
|
option
.option
==
ColumnOption
::
NotNull
);
let
has_default
=
column_def
.options
.iter
()
.any
(|
option
|
matches!
(
option
.option
,
ColumnOption
::
Default
(
_
)));
if
has_not_null
&&
!
has_default
{
self
.error
=
Some
(
format!
(
"Column `{name}.{}` is NOT NULL, but no DEFAULT value was configured!"
,
column_def
.name

ControlFlow

data.title: Certified randomness using a trapped-ion quantum processor
data.author: wahsmail
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种利用56量子比特的Quantinuum H2-1离子阱量子计算机，通过互联网生成可验证随机比特的方法。该方法基于随机电路采样（RCS）的经典计算难度，允许客户端使用少量随机种子生成量子“挑战”电路，发送给不受信任的量子服务器执行，并验证服务器结果。通过经典验证，结合多台超级计算机的计算能力，我们在限制性近似敌手模型下认证了71,313比特的随机熵。这种方法展示了当前量子计算机在实际应用中的潜力，特别是在需要可验证随机数的场合，如信息安全和公平性保障等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算应用的实际价值与合理性

不同观点：
• 观点一：质疑量子计算应用的实际价值。非随机字符（nonrandomstring）认为，一个成本仅为0.05美元的普通锗二极管（OA91）就能实现同样的功能，质疑是否真的需要用量子计算来解决这个问题。这表明对量子计算应用的实用性持怀疑态度，暗示可能存在为了追求量子计算热潮而强行应用的情况。

• 观点二：潜在的反驳或补充。虽然没有直接在评论中表达，但可以推测，有人可能认为即使是简单的器件，量子计算的应用研究有助于推动技术前沿发展，而不应仅仅根据个别器件的成本来评判整个研究领域的价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：量子计算应用的合理性与实际需求之间的矛盾。非随机字符的评论反映了一种对量子计算领域过度炒作的担忧，认为某些应用可能没有实际必要性，只是为了追逐科技潮流。

• 论据和例子：非随机字符举例说明一个廉价的传统二极管就能完成相似功能，暗示没有必要使用复杂的量子技术来解决简单问题，从而质疑该领域的研究动机和资金投入的合理性。

43484100.article_content:
Certified randomness using a trapped-ion quantum processor
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Computer science
Quantum information
Qubits
Abstract
Although quantum computers can perform a wide range of practically important tasks beyond the abilities of classical computers
1
,
2
, realizing this potential remains a challenge. An example is to use an untrusted remote device to generate random bits that can be certified to contain a certain amount of entropy
3
. Certified randomness has many applications but is impossible to achieve solely by classical computation. Here we demonstrate the generation of certifiably random bits using the 56-qubit Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer accessed over the Internet. Our protocol leverages the classical hardness of recent random circuit sampling demonstrations
4
,
5
: a client generates quantum ‘challenge’ circuits using a small randomness seed, sends them to an untrusted quantum server to execute and verifies the results of the server. We analyse the security of our protocol against a restricted class of realistic near-term adversaries. Using classical verification with measured combined sustained performance of 1.1 × 10
18
floating-point operations per second across multiple supercomputers, we certify 71,313 bits of entropy under this restricted adversary and additional assumptions. Our results demonstrate a step towards the practical applicability of present-day quantum computers.
Similar content being viewed by others

Article
Open access

Article
Open access
24 February 2021

Article
03 August 2023
Main
In recent years, numerous theoretical results have shown evidence that quantum computers have the potential to tackle a wide range of problems out of reach of classical techniques. The main examples include factoring large integers
6
, implicitly solving exponentially sized systems of linear equations
7
, optimizing intractable problems
8
, learning certain functions
9
and simulating large quantum many-body systems
10
. However, accounting for considerations such as quantum error correction overheads and gate speeds, the resource requirements of known quantum algorithms for these problems put them far outside the reach of near-term quantum devices, including many suggested fault-tolerant architectures. Consequently, it is unclear whether the devices available in the near term can benefit a practical application
11
.
Starting with one of the first ‘quantum supremacy’ demonstrations
5
, several groups have used random circuit sampling (RCS) as an example of a task that can be executed faster and with a lower energy cost on present-day quantum computers compared with what is achievable classically
4
,
12
,
13
,
14
. Yet, despite rapid experimental progress, a beyond-classical demonstration of a practically useful task performed by gate-based quantum computers has so far remained unknown.
Random number generation is a natural task for the beyond-classical demonstration because randomness is intrinsic to quantum mechanics, and it is important in many applications, ranging from information security to ensuring the fairness of processes such as jury selection

data.title: Some Reflections After a Month of Tracking My Own Online Activity
data.author: mcwhittemore
data.article_summary: Matthew Whittemore使用自定义浏览器扩展程序记录了一个月以来的浏览活动，发现他花费大量时间在网页上，尤其是处理电子邮件。他列出了访问时长最多的12个网站，前几名包括Gmail、LinkedIn、Feedbin等。他惊讶地发现，实际使用互联网的方式与自己预期的不同，例如他原以为自己花很多时间阅读Wikipedia，但实际上在Google Docs上花费了几乎同等时间。他还提到对职业选择和自我认知的思考，认为人们常根据“酷”或“成功”选择工作，但这些工作可能并不令人满足。此外，Matthew希望Feedbin能改进文章链接方式，并计划进一步分析浏览模式。他承认数据可能不完全准确，且无法在手机或工作电脑上获取类似数据。
data.comments_summary:

43482468.article_content:
Matthew Whittemore
Page Activity
Since 8:38 PM on February 22nd, I’ve been recording all my browsing activity in a database I manage using a custom-built browser extension and a wrapper around
@rosskevin/ifvisible
. The result? I now have a clear picture of just how much time I’ve spent on the web this past month. And, well… I spend a lot of time reading email. Go figure.
Here are the top 12 domains I visited, ranked by active time spent on them:
mail.google.com
linkedin.com
feedbin.com
github.com
local-files (file://, aka, me hacking old-school serverless)
youtube.com
mcwhittemore.com (turns out I spent a lot of time on my own site...)
chatgpt.com
en.wikipedia.org
docs.google.com
news.ycombinator.com
www.themag.co.uk
Looking over this list, I’m surprised at how different my actual internet usage is from how I thought I used the internet. Gmail, LinkedIn, and Feedbin all make sense near the top (though I’m surprised LinkedIn is so high), but I didn’t expect GitHub, ChatGPT, and Google Docs to take up as much time as they did. I’ve always considered myself someone who spends a lot of time reading Wikipedia and Newcastle news (
www.themag.co.uk
), but in reality, I was almost as active in Google Docs as I was on Wikipedia. Making this point is totally why I included 12 domains rather than, say, 5.
A Side Note
This ties into a theme I’ve been thinking about lately. In short, I’ve been pondering if we identify more with who we think we are than with who we actually are. The idea came up while reading
Every Good Endeavor
. In it, Tim Keller notes that many people take jobs based on what’s considered cool or successful, only to find them draining because the work itself isn’t fulfilling. I tend to agree with his point. Picking a career is a weird thing. I also think the idea applies beyond career choices. It’s here in the disconnect the version of me in my head as someone who spends lots of time reading Wikipedia when, in reality, I spend nearly as much time playing with spreadsheets in Google Docs. Yes, that doesn’t mean I don’t read a good amount of Wikipedia, but, clearly, I do a lot more than that with my web browser.
Feedbin
I wish I had started tracking my browsing a little earlier—I’d love to see how adding Feedbin changed my internet habits. I also really wish Feedbin used distinct URIs for each feed item as I read it! Right now, my tracking shows that I spent 4 hours and 22 minutes on Feedbin’s homepage since I signed up on February 28th, just aimlessly clicking around. My total time on the domain was 4 hours and 28 minutes, which means almost all of it was spent at /. What gives?!
This is now on my growing list of things I wish Feedbin did. Ideally, it wouldn’t even need to be a unique-to-me URL—just something I could share so that another Feedbin user (most likely future me) could open the same article. Future me would love that.
A Few Closing Notes
I’m not calling this data “Activity” because I’m not entirely sure how well my hacked-together browser tracker handles reading sessions. It’s possible that long-form content appears as a bunch of short sessions. In aggregate (since every time I scroll, a new session starts), it should be fairly accurate. But less interactive pages will likely have some lost time.
I had string of days recently without opening Feedbin. I’m curious if I can group the data by day and categorize my browsing patterns, detecting ebbs and flows in usage like this. What did I do instead? Maybe I read a book.
Most of my local-files time (2 hours, 41 minutes) was spent working on (or playing with)
Web Graph Browser
. It’s a kind of dumb, kind of fun, totally hacked-together tool that lets you “browse” the “web” by clicking nodes in a graph (links) to see how pages connect.
All this data is for just my personal laptop. It would be so interesting to have this for my phone too, but mobile browsers hate extensions. It would also be so interesting to have this for my work as well, but... well... I suspect explaining that extension would be interesting if IT ever reviewed me, so we won’t get that data.

data.title: Trump pardons Nikola founder Trevor Milton in securities fraud case
data.author: Ozarkian
data.article_summary: 美国前总统唐纳德·特朗普赦免了Nikola公司创始人特雷弗·米尔顿，后者因在2022年被判欺诈投资者罪，与电动及氢动力卡车业务的成功造假有关，被判处四年监禁，但一直在上诉期间保持自由。特朗普的赦免使得米尔顿无需支付6.8亿美元的赔偿金，也免除了进一步的法律追责。米尔顿将自己形容为被政府不公正对待的受害者，并将自己的案件与特朗普面临的法律问题相比较。在获得赦免前，米尔顿曾向特朗普及其政治盟友捐赠了大笔资金。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对特朗普政策及其影响的评价与争议

不同观点：
• [对特朗普行为的批评] 用户cma强烈批评特朗普的行为，尤其是其在对中国征收关税时的理由与随后对Ross Ulbricht的赦免之间的矛盾。cma指出特朗普曾以打击毒品为由实施关税，但随后却赦免了大规模的毒品运营商，这种行为被认为是自相矛盾和不道德的。此外，cma提到特朗普在上一任期内还赦免了涉及监狱腐败的法官，进一步质疑其公正性与道德标准。

• [无关政治的评论] 用户plut9和blitzar的评论并未直接涉及政治立场或特朗普的政策，而是通过讽刺和夸张的方式表达对高昂价格的不满（"All downhill from here" 和 "All for the low, low price of $1,670,000"），可能是对某些经济现象或市场价格的调侃。

补充讨论：
• [赦免的争议] 用户cma特别提到了特朗普对Ross Ulbricht和涉腐法官的赦免，认为这些行为反映出特朗普在利用总统权力进行交易（selling pardons），质疑其赦免行为的合法性与正当性。

• [讨论焦点] 争议的焦点在于特朗普政策的矛盾性及其赦免行为的正当性。cma的评论引发了对特朗普执政期间行为的道德与法律层面的质疑，而其他用户的评论则没有深入讨论这些具体问题，而是通过讽刺表达对其他问题的关注。

Key Points
President Donald Trump pardoned Nikola founder Trevor Milton.
Milton was convicted in October 2022 of crimes related to defrauding investors with misrepresentations about the success of the electric- and hydrogen-powered truck maker.
The former CEO was sentenced to four years in prison, but has been free pending appeal of his conviction in New York federal court.
Nikola filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in February.

Trump pardons Nikola founder in securities fraud case
Squawk on the Street
President
Donald Trump
pardoned
Nikola Corp.
founder
Trevor Milton
for his 2022 conviction of federal crimes related to defrauding
investors
with false claims about the success of the electric and hydrogen-powered
truck maker
.
Milton, 42, was sentenced in December 2023 to four years in
prison
, but he has been free since then pending an appeal of the former CEO's criminal conviction on
securities
and wire
fraud
charges in
U.S. District Court in Manhattan
.
The pardon came two weeks after federal prosecutors urged District Court Judge Edgardo Ramos to order Milton to pay
restitution
of $680 million to Nikola shareholders, and another $15.2 million to Peter Hicks, a victim of his wire fraud.
Because of the pardon, Ramos now cannot order restitution of any kind.
Trevor Milton, founder of Nikola Corp., arrives at court in New York, on Monday, Sept. 12, 2022.
Victor J. Blue | Bloomberg | Getty Images
"Oh my gosh, oh, you won't believe what just happened," Milton said in an
Instagram
video posted on his personal account Thursday. "Probably the best day I've had in five years."
"I just got a call from the president of the United States, on my phone, and he signed my full and unconditional pardon of innocence," said Milton, who appeared to be driving a vehicle in the video.
"I am free. The prosecutors can no longer hurt me," he said. "They can't destroy my family, they can't rip everything away from me, they can't ruin my life."
The White House confirmed the pardon.
Trump later Friday was asked why he granted Milton a pardon.
"I think he was exonerated," Trump said told reporters at the White House. "And then they brought him into New York, he had a rough, rough road, and ... he was exonerated. It was a big celebration. "
Milton was
convicted
at trial in October 2022.
"They say the thing that he did wrong was, he was one of the first people that supported a gentleman named Donald Trump for president," Trump said. "He supported Trump. He liked Trump. I didn't know him, but he liked him."
Trump went on to say of Milton, "They persecuted him, they destroyed five years of his life. He ... fought for five years of his life, and he did nothing wrong."
"And he's a good person."
Defense attorneys for Milton did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Milton, in a statement, said that one of his lawyers, Bradley Bondi, did not work on his application for a pardon.
Bondi is the brother of U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi, who was appointed to her post by Trump.
A spokesman for the Manhattan U.S. Attorney's Office, which prosecuted Milton, declined to comment on the pardon.
The Manhattan U.S. Attorney's Office, when it obtained an indictment against Milton in 2021, said some investors defrauded by his scheme "suffered tens and even hundreds of thousands of dollars in losses, including, in certain cases, the loss of their retirement savings or funds that they had borrowed to invest in Nikola."

• [对特朗普行为的批评] 用户cma强烈批评特朗普的行为，尤其是其在对中国征收关税时的理由与随后对Ross Ulbricht的赦免之间的矛盾。cma指出特朗普曾以打击毒品为由实施关税，但随后却赦免了大规模的毒品运营商，这种行为被认为是自相矛盾和不道德的。此外，cma提到特朗普在上一任期内还赦免了涉及监狱腐败的法官，进一步质疑其公正性与道德标准。

• [无关政治的评论] 用户plut9和blitzar的评论并未直接涉及政治立场或特朗普的政策，而是通过讽刺和夸张的方式表达对高昂价格的不满（"All downhill from here" 和 "All for the low, low price of $1,670,000"），可能是对某些经济现象或市场价格的调侃。

补充讨论：
• [赦免的争议] 用户cma特别提到了特朗普对Ross Ulbricht和涉腐法官的赦免，认为这些行为反映出特朗普在利用总统权力进行交易（selling pardons），质疑其赦免行为的合法性与正当性。

• [讨论焦点] 争议的焦点在于特朗普政策的矛盾性及其赦免行为的正当性。cma的评论引发了对特朗普执政期间行为的道德与法律层面的质疑，而其他用户的评论则没有深入讨论这些具体问题，而是通过讽刺表达对其他问题的关注。

data.title: Plain – a web framework for building products with Python
data.author: brylie
data.article_summary: Plain 是一个基于 Python 的 web 框架，是 Django 的分支，旨在引入新想法并保持 Python 生态系统的成熟模式。它支持通过单条命令进行本地开发并快速上线，包含多个独立可选的包，如处理 URL、视图、模板、表单、缓存、电子邮件、会话、后台任务和 JSON API 等功能。Plain 还提供认证包，支持传统和现代登录方式，如密码和 OAuth。其管理包允许自定义管理后台和功能标志控制，开发包优化本地开发体验，前端包则集成现代工具如 Tailwind 和 HTMX。Plain 被设计用于构建新业务、内部工具或个人项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Django框架及其分支Plain框架的优缺点与未来发展方向

不同观点：
• **支持Plain框架的观点**：
  - [miiiiiike] 认为Django需要像Angular一样复兴，当前社区太小且封闭，需要更多贡献者。对Django现有问题感到担忧，认为需要采取行动，哪怕是通过分叉。
  - [petr25102018] 理解Plain作为分叉的存在，认为Django领导层未能突破旧范式，Plain或其他第三方应用的尝试是有价值的。

• **反对Plain框架的观点**：
  - [theptip] 不理解为什么要分叉Django，认为Django的ORM和生态系统是其强项，分叉会破坏兼容性，建议通过Django项目模板实现改进。
  - [sroerick] 对Plain的“为什么”感到困惑，认为Django的不足可以通过现有生态系统（如Celery和Django REST）解决，分叉可能增加复杂性。
  - [999900000999] 对Plain持混合态度，认为Django的插件生态和文档支持无可替代，不希望看到一个由单人维护的分叉。
  - [spapas82] 认为Plain的所谓创新已经在Django核心或可靠的第三方包中实现，分叉可能分裂社区，不如将努力用于改进Django。
  - [mcdirty] 认为Plain的文档和维护者较少，投资风险大。
  - [jgb1984] 表示会继续使用Django，对Plain不感兴趣。

• **对Django的批评与改进建议**：
  - [mariocesar] 对Plain分叉感到不安，认为这是在绕过Django的集体努力，担心Plain可能走向商业化或狭隘的方向，但同时也感到被推动更积极参与Django贡献。
  - [nop_slide] 认为Django在DX和功能上落后于Laravel和Rails，生态系统碎片化，配置复杂，文档不够完善，希望Django能更完整。
  - [askonomm] 对Django设置中使用字符串引用类的方式不满，认为这导致无法轻松导航和使用自动完成功能。

• **技术细节与安装问题**：
  - [JodieBenitez] 在尝试运行Plain的入门套件时遇到SSL证书下载失败和需要输入密码的问题，建议将SSL设为可选。

补充讨论：
• **关于Django社区和贡献**：
  - [miiiiiike] 提到Django社区小且紧密，外人很难参与，感觉需要等待而不是主动贡献。
  - [mariocesar] 表示对Django的热爱，希望社区能更开放和尊重贡献。

• **关于分叉与创新的讨论**：
  - [scottpersinger] 建议从FastAPI等现代框架开始，而不是分叉Django。
  - [mychael] 认为Plain的独特价值不明显，只是对Django的简单替换。

争议焦点：
• Plain框架是否有必要分叉Django，以及分叉是否会导致Django社区的分裂和生态系统的破坏。
• Django当前的不足是否可以通过现有生态系统和第三方包解决，还是需要通过分叉或重大改进来实现。

总结：
评论中对于Plain框架的分叉存在明显分歧，一方认为Django需要重大改进甚至分叉，另一方则认为Django的强项在于其生态系统和兼容性，分叉可能弊大于利。同时，对Django社区的封闭性和贡献难度也有所批评。

Plain
A web framework for building products with Python.
Clone a starter kit →
Leverage the world's most popular
programming language
Plain is a fork of
Django
,
bringing new ideas to established patterns in the Python landscape.
Build a new business, an internal tool, or something for yourself.
Entrepreneurial
Plain was forked inside of
PullApprove
— a revenue-generating SaaS with Fortune 500 customers.
End-to-end
Local development with a
single command
.
Go to production with dashboards, feature flags, and more.
Ecosystem
Plain is split into multiple
first-party packages
.
Major features are optional and new ideas can evolve independently.
Foundation Packages
Building blocks for products
plain
The foundations for shipping Python code to the web — urls, views, templates, forms, and more.
plain.models
Store your data in Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite with a tried and true ORM.
plain.cache
A caching solution designed just to work with your existing database.
plain.email
App-wide email configuration and sending, with templates and attachments.
plain.sessions
Read and write to database-backed sessions.
plain.worker
An official solution for background work, backed by the database you already have.
plain.api
Build JSON APIs with the same class-based view architecture you already know.
Browse source docs →
Auth Packages
Authentication you can trust (and host yourself)
plain.auth
The foundation for adding users to your app, authenticating them to requests and restricting views.
plain.oauth
A flexible OAuth solution to support modern social logins and API access.
plain.passwords
Password-based login that works like it always has, if you want it.
plain.loginlink
Send one-time login links to users, and let them log in without a password.
plain.passkeys
coming soon
Passwordless login with passkeys.
Browse source docs →
Admin Packages
The backbone of your back office
plain.admin
An admin dashboard you can fully customize, and Plain packages know how to integrate with.
plain.flags
Database-backed feature flags to control who sees what and quietly deploy progress.
plain.support
Provide better customer support without the need for third-party services.
plain.redirection
Monitor 404s and manage redirects in the database.
plain.pageviews
See what users are looking at, and provide better support.
Browse source docs →
Dev Packages
A tailored local development experience
plain.dev
Fire up your local development environment with a single command.
plain.pytest
Write and run tests with one of Python's most popular testing libraries.
plain.code
Format and lint your Python code with opinionated defaults.
plain.tunnel
Expose your local app to the internet to build webhook integrations.
Browse source docs →
Frontend Packages
Modern tools for modern user interfaces
plain.tailwind
First-class integration for everyone's favorite CSS framework. Node.js not required.
plain.htmx
Build a modern user experience with the tools you already know.
plain.elements
A new paradigm for reusable components across your app's templates.
plain.pages
File-based routing for marketing sites and documentation, using HTML and Markdown.
plain.esbuild
A simplified build process for JavaScript that needs to be compiled.
plain.vendor
Download and self-host JavaScript and CSS assets without depending on a CDN.
Browse source docs →

data.title: Rust Any part 3: we have upcasts
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: Armin Ronacher在2025年3月27日的博客文章中讨论了Rust 1.86版本如何解决了"upcasting"问题。三年前，他分享了一个名为"As-Any Hack"的技巧，以在稳定版的Rust中实现向上转型（upcasting）到超traits。具体问题是在使用如`DebugAny`这种继承自`Any`的trait时，无法在`dyn DebugAny`上调用`Any`的方法，如`downcast_ref`，导致编译错误。随着Rust 1.86的发布，这个问题得到了修复，现在可以正常进行转型和方法调用。这一更新意味着许多旧的技巧可以被淘汰，但需要根据最低支持的Rust版本来调整。Ronacher对参与修复这一问题的开发者表示感谢。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust语言中的trait继承与多trait实现的机制及其与传统面向对象编程（OO）语言的区别。

不同观点：
• **kibwen的观点**：Rust中的trait不是传统面向对象语言中的“继承”关系，而是“依赖”关系。一个trait可以“要求”另一个trait，但这不意味着方法的继承，而是实现上的前提条件。因此，不能用传统OO语言中的继承概念来理解Rust的trait关系。

• **trashface的观点**：提出在Rust中如果一个类型可能实现多个trait（如A, B, C），是否必须全部实现这些trait的问题。他希望有一个基础trait对象，可以查询是否支持其他trait，而不必为不支持的trait实现stub。这类似于C++中的dynamic_cast功能，但由于Rust没有继承，目前可能无法实现。

• **mmastrac的观点**：提到Rust的vtable布局变化，现在可以保证supertrait的布局在方法前缀中是可预测的，或者提供指向合适vtable的指针。他认为这可能与菱形trait继承有关。

• **the__alchemist的观点**：表达了对文章内容的不解，尽管使用Rust多年，仍不清楚文章描述的内容。

• **fcantournet的观点**：简单提问，带有调侃性质，询问某个类型是否是Debug或DebugAny。

• **aerzen的观点**：喜欢Rust的原因是Any类型使用起来不方便，这促使开发者使用静态类型实现，从而推动更合理的代码设计。

• **jtrueb的观点**：认为Rust正在逐渐接近面向对象编程（OOP），暗示Rust可能在某些方面变得更像传统OO语言。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Rust的trait机制与传统OO语言继承机制的区别，以及在多trait实现和查询支持的其他trait时的实现难度。
• 不同用户对Rust的复杂性、类型系统及其与传统OO语言的差异有不同的理解和期待，部分用户对文章内容和技术细节感到困惑。
• 部分用户关注Rust的演变，尤其是其与OOP的接近程度，反映了Rust在语言设计上可能正在经历的变化。

43523238.article_content:
Armin Ronacher
's Thoughts and Writings
blog
archive
tags
projects
talks
about
Rust Any Part 3: Finally we have Upcasts
written on Thursday, March 27, 2025
Three years ago I shared the
As-Any Hack
on
this blog.  That hack is a way to get upcasting to supertraits working on
stable Rust.  To refresh your memory, the goal was to make something like
this work:
#[derive(Debug)]
struct
AnyBox
(
Box
<
dyn
DebugAny
>
);
trait
DebugAny
:
Any
+
Debug
{}
impl
<
T
:
Any
+
Debug
+
'
static
>
DebugAny
for
T
{}
The problem? Even though
DebugAny
inherits from
Any
, Rust wouldn't let you
use methods from
Any
on a
dyn DebugAny
.  So while you could call
DebugAny
methods just fine, trying to use
downcast_ref
from
Any
(the
reason to use Any in the first place) would fail:
fn
main
()
{
let
any_box
=
AnyBox
(
Box
::
new
(
42
i32
));
dbg!
(
any_box
.
0.
downcast_ref
::
<
i32
>
());
// Compile error
}
The same would happen if we tried to cast it into an
&dyn Any
?  A
compile error again:
fn
main
()
{
let
any_box
=
AnyBox
(
Box
::
new
(
42
i32
));
let
any
=
&*
any_box
.
0
as
&
dyn
Any
;
dbg!
(
any
.
downcast_ref
::
<
i32
>
());
}
But there is good news!  As of Rust 1.86, this is finally fixed. The cast
now works:
[src/main.rs:14:5] any.downcast_ref::<i32>() = Some(
42,
)
At the time of writing, this fix is in the beta channel, but stable
release is just around the corner.  That means a lot of old hacks can
finally be retired.  At least once your MSRV moves up.
Thank you so much to everyone who
worked on this
to make it work!

• 部分用户关注Rust的演变，尤其是其与OOP的接近程度，反映了Rust在语言设计上可能正在经历的变化。

data.title: The average college student today
data.author: Jyaif
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高等教育中的出勤率、学习态度、教学质量以及技术（如AI）对教育的影响

不同观点：
• joshdavham 认为，学生缺勤是因为课堂内容常常只是照本宣科，学生觉得参加讲座浪费时间，不如自学。他提到自己和兄弟在大学期间也经常逃课但依然成绩优异，表明有些课程的讲座确实没有太大价值。

• jt-hill 持批评态度，认为学生将大学教育视为纯粹的交易，只为获得文凭而不是为了学习。他指出，大多数学生并不真正关心学习本身，因此不愿意在课堂上投入时间。

• mrbonner 通过工作中的文档写作文化类比，讨论了技术（如LLM）如何改变学习和工作方式。他提出，技术可以简化流程，但也可能导致一些传统技能的退化，例如深入的文档写作和阅读。

• Nifty3929 提出通过入学考试筛选学生，以确保学生具备成功完成课程的基础知识，避免浪费双方的时间。这一观点强调了学术标准的维持和有效利用教学资源。

• martindbp 对整个教育系统的目的提出质疑，认为在互联网和AI时代，传统教育体系的价值正在下降。他指出，教育在知识获取、社交、职业准备等方面的功能可以被其他方式替代。

• flakiness 对比了日本和美国的学生文化，指出美国学生在经济成功背景下可能失去了对学习的认真态度，而日本学生依然努力学习。

• andrewvc 提到学生使用手机对学习的影响，建议在K-12阶段全面禁止手机以提高注意力和学习效果。

• JimBlackwood 认为，出勤率和参与度的下降与疫情后的变化和简化的课程有关，并质疑在当前社会如何保持高学术标准。

• Herring 提供了PISA成绩的数据，指出美国在阅读和科学方面的表现相对稳定，但在数学方面有所下降，试图通过数据分析提供一些背景信息。

• DeathArrow 强调了竞争的重要性，认为应保持高学术标准，并通过竞争筛选出真正有能力的学生，而不是让所有人都能轻松毕业。

• Ukv 讨论了学生要求提供讲义的合理性，认为这在不同大学和院系可能有所不同，但在他自己的经历中，讲义通常会在虚拟学习环境中提前提供。

• austin-cheney 指出了学生阅读和写作能力下降的问题，认为这与他们缺乏实践和过度依赖技术有关，特别是在软件开发领域。

• kebsup 支持通过在线资源获取更好的教学质量，认为传统的黑板教学已经不能满足学生的需求，尤其是在有更高质量的在线资源可供选择的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于学生对课堂和学习的重视程度，以及技术对传统教育模式的冲击。部分评论者认为学生将大学视为交易，缺乏学习动力，而另一些人则认为技术的发展提供了更多有效的学习途径，传统教育模式需要适应和变革。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是学术标准的维持和筛选机制，如何通过考试或其他方式确保学生具备必要的基础知识和能力，以提高教学效果和学生的学习体验。

data.title: It's five grand a day to miss our S3 exit
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了37signals公司计划在今年6月30日之前将数据从AWS S3迁移到自建数据中心的Pure Storage系统，以节省每年近150万美元的成本。目前，他们存储了18PB数据，并获得了AWS提供的免费60天数据迁出窗口，避免了高额的迁出费用。尽管数据传输需要约三周时间，但若未按时完成，他们将面临每天5000美元的额外支出。整体来看，使用Pure Storage在五年内可节省约500万美元，硬件成本为150万美元，支持和保修费用不到100万美元。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：云服务与自建基础设施的成本与效益分析

不同观点：
• **云服务的成本合理性**：
   - **ifightcrime**：云服务一直以来都比较贵，但你为便利和速度付费。当公司发展到一定规模时，成本问题会变得突出。可以通过前期架构和供应商选择来缓解，但这不是新问题。
   - **rvz**：云服务成本累积迅速，特别是当团队低估成本时。AWS等云供应商的定价机制会导致即使在少量使用情况下也会产生高额费用。

• **自建基础设施的成本效益**：
   - **comrade1234**：通过对比硬件和托管成本与AWS价格，发现自建基础设施的回本期约为三年。AWS会根据硬件成本调整价格。
   - **npalli**：通过建模发现，从S3迁移到自建设施的回本期可能长达18年，即使考虑折旧周期仍需8年。初始硬件成本和后续运营费用较高。

• **功能与需求匹配**：
   - **andrewaylett**：AWS S3提供更多功能和弹性，如果不需要这些功能，可以避免额外费用。但需要确保支付的费用与需求匹配。
   - **otterley**：建议使用S3智能分层以降低成本，特别是对于访问频率不高的数据。

• **具体实施与技术选择**：
   - **theptip**：Basecamp作为一个自建基础设施的典型例子，因其非风投支持且工程能力强，租赁云服务的灵活性需求较低。
   - **albert_e**：逐步迁移数据并删除S3上的数据可以提前开始节省成本，前提是数据消费者能够适应。
   - **Axsuul**：担心自建基础设施的硬件故障处理不如云服务优雅，可能导致严重停机。

• **技术细节与系统性能**：
   - **siscia**：关注新系统的具体技术指标，如每GB成本、读写延迟、并发支持和最大吞吐量。

补充讨论：
• **供应商反应**：
   - **tgtweak**：提到如果告知云供应商离开，有时会给予一定回扣，令人感到不满。

• **硬件选择**：
   - **DeathArrow**：认为使用SSD是浪费，建议使用传统硬盘和RAID结构，质疑AWS是否仅使用SSD。

争议焦点：
• 云服务的高成本与自建基础设施的长期效益之间的权衡。
• 不同技术选择（如SSD vs HDD，S3 vs 自建存储）在成本和性能上的优劣。

总结：评论中对云服务与自建基础设施的成本效益有明显分歧，主要围绕具体需求、功能匹配、技术选择和实施细节展开讨论。

43489698.article_content:
March 26, 2025
It's five grand a day to miss our S3 exit
We're spending just shy of $1.5 million/year on AWS S3 at the moment to host files for
Basecamp
,
HEY
, and
everything else
. The only way we were able to get the pricing that low was by signing a four-year contract. That contract expires this summer, June 30, so that's our departure date for the final leg of
our cloud exit
.
We've already racked the replacement from
Pure Storage
in our two primary data centers. A combined 18 petabytes, securely replicated a thousand miles apart. It's a gorgeous rack full of blazing-fast NVMe storage modules. Each card in the chassis
capable of storing 150TB now
.
Pure Storage comes with an S3-compatible API, so no need for CEPH, Minio, or any of the other object storage software solutions you might need, if you were trying to do this exercise on commodity hardware. This makes it pretty easy from the app side to do the swap.
But there's still work to do. We have to transfer almost six petabytes out of S3. In an earlier age, that egress alone would have cost hundreds of thousands of dollars in fees alone. But now AWS offers
a free 60-day egress window
for anyone who wants to leave, so that drops the cost to $0. Nice!
It takes a while to transfer that much data, though. Even on the fat 40-Gbit pipe we have set aside for the purpose, it'll probably take at least three weeks, once you factor in overhead and some babysitting of the process.
That's when it's good to remind ourselves why June 30th matters. And the reminder math pens out in nice, round numbers for easy recollection: If we don't get this done in time, we'll be paying a cool
five thousand dollars a day
to continue to use S3 (if all the files are still there). Yikes!
That's $35,000/week! That's $150,000/month!
Pretty serious money for a company of our size. But so are the savings. Over five years, it'll now be almost five million! Maybe even more, depending on the growth in files we need to store for customers. About $1.5 million for the Pure Storage hardware, and a bit less than a million over five years for warranty and support.
But those big numbers always seem a bit abstract to me. The idea of paying $5,000/day, if we miss our departure date, is awfully concrete in comparison.

data.title: Sim Daltonism: The color blindness simulator
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: Sim Daltonism是一款色盲模拟器，帮助用户从色盲患者的视角感知颜色。该应用有iOS和Mac版本，可通过iOS设备的摄像头或Mac应用的屏幕过滤功能，模拟不同类型色盲的视觉效果。该应用是开源的，用户可以查看源码并贡献代码。此外，该应用由Michel Fortin开发，他还提供了其他应用程序和相关服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发者工具中的颜色模拟功能及其应用场景

不同观点：
• [oniony] 认为Android的开发者选项中的颜色空间模拟功能可以用来体验色盲视角，甚至可以用在相机上查看现实世界的效果。
• [AprilArcus] 提出反向应用的可能性，即通过调整颜色来矫正色觉障碍，比如增强红色或减弱绿色和蓝色，以模拟P3色域外的视觉效果。
• [bluechair] 引用开发者的说明，指出颜色盲模拟仅是近似，不能完美呈现色盲患者的真实视觉体验，且每个人的色觉差异以及设备光谱响应不同。作为色盲患者，他认为目前没有模拟器能准确还原他的视觉体验。
• [rollcat] 分享了个人使用iPhone颜色滤镜的经验，尤其是灰度滤镜对其注意力和情绪的影响，并建议颜色滤镜可以像音频压缩器一样更灵活。
• [DawsonBruce] 强调该工具在GUI设计中的实用性，帮助设计者考虑不同色觉用户的需求。
• [egypturnash] 认为该工具在艺术创作中非常有用，尤其在检查对比度时经常使用。
• [lastdong] 赞赏该应用的优化程度，尤其是iOS版本仅有444KB的大小。
• [machine_ghost] 对Mac独占表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 颜色模拟工具的实际效果存在争议，特别是[bluechair]作为色盲患者认为没有模拟器能准确还原其视觉体验。
• [rollcat] 提供了个人对颜色滤镜的主观感受和改进建议，讨论了滤镜对用户体验的长期影响。
• 工具的应用场景多样，包括GUI设计和艺术创作中的对比度检查。

From the perspective of a color blind person, some colors are impossible to distinguish. Sim Daltonism lets you visualize colors as they are perceived with various types of color blindness. Use the camera on your iOS device, or use the Mac app to filter a region of the screen.
Sim Daltonism is
open source
. Take a look and contribute code if you like.
